A court case. A civil proceeding is either an action, usually started by a statement of claim, or an application, started by a notice of application.
```

### `glossary:proceeding:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "proceeding" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Small Claims cases are actions, started by filing a plaintiff's claim.
```

### `glossary:proceeding:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "proceeding" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Family courts usually say "case". A case means an application or other way of bringing a matter to court, including all its motions, enforcements and appeals.
```

### `glossary:process-server`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "process server"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
A person who serves court documents on others professionally, for a fee. Using one is optional; a friend or business associate can also serve documents. It can help when the person to be served is far away or service could be awkward or confrontational. Whoever serves the document signs and swears or affirms the affidavit of service.
```

### `glossary:proof-of-service`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "proof of service"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/document/guide-procedures-small-claims-court/serving-documents

```
A document that shows the court that another party was properly given (served with) a court document. It is usually an affidavit of service: a sworn or affirmed statement by the person who did the serving, saying who was served, when and how. Lawyers, and in Small Claims and family cases paralegals, can instead sign a certificate of service. Many documents must be filed together with proof of service.
```

### `glossary:proof-of-service:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "proof of service" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/document/guide-procedures-small-claims-court/serving-documents

```
Use an Affidavit of Service (Form 8A). A lawyer or paralegal can use a certificate of service (Form 8B).
```

### `glossary:proof-of-service:civil`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "proof of service" (in civil cases in the superior court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/document/guide-procedures-small-claims-court/serving-documents

```
Use an Affidavit of Service (Form 16B). A lawyer can use a lawyer's certificate of service (Form 16B.1).
```

### `glossary:proof-of-service:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "proof of service" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/document/guide-procedures-small-claims-court/serving-documents

```
An affidavit of service is Form 6B. A lawyer or paralegal can use a certificate of service (Form 6C). Service can also be proved in other ways, such as a written acceptance of service or the signed return postcard when a document is mailed with one.
```

### `glossary:property-claim`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "property claim"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/990114

```
A family court claim about property. It covers a claim to equalize net family property between married spouses, a claim that a partner holds property partly for you (a constructive or resulting trust), and a claim for money because the other person was unjustly enriched at your expense.
```

### `glossary:provisional-order`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "provisional order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/990114

```
A family support order that has no effect until another court confirms it. An Ontario court can make one when the person who would pay support lives in another province, territory or country (a "reciprocating jurisdiction") that needs this kind of order. The Ontario court sends it there to be confirmed.
```

### `glossary:recipient`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "recipient"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/990114

```
A family law term for the person entitled to receive money, such as support or costs, under a court order or agreement. It includes a parent who receives child support for a child. It can also be an agency or children's aid society owed money, an expert owed fees, or the estate trustee of someone who was owed money.
```

### `glossary:registrar`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "registrar"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A court official who runs the court office and handles court files. In the Superior Court, the local registrar can do some things without a judge, such as signing a default judgment for a fixed amount of money or transferring a case to Small Claims Court when everyone agrees.
```

### `glossary:registrar:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "registrar" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Small Claims Court has a clerk instead, who can make certain orders when all parties consent.
```

### `glossary:registrar:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "registrar" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The family rules use "clerk", meaning a person with the authority of a clerk or registrar of the court.
```

### `glossary:release`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "release"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
A document the parties sign to confirm that they are giving up some or all of their claims connected with the dispute. It is usually signed as part of a settlement.
```

### `glossary:representative`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "representative"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
The person who acts for a party in a court case, such as a lawyer or paralegal. If you have no representative, you are self-represented and do the steps yourself.
```

### `glossary:representative:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "representative" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Your representative can be a lawyer, a paralegal or another person, but only someone the Law Society Act allows to act as a representative.
```

### `glossary:representative:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "representative" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A "licensed representative" is a lawyer or a family legal services provider. Anyone else can represent you only if the court gives permission in advance.
```

### `glossary:respondent`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "respondent"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The person on the other side of an application or an appeal: the one the case is brought against. The person who starts an application is the applicant; the person who starts an appeal is the appellant.
```

### `glossary:respondent:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "respondent" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Small Claims cases use plaintiff and defendant instead.
```

### `glossary:respondent:civil`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "respondent" (in civil cases in the superior court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A respondent is the person an application is made against, or the person an appeal is brought against. Actions use plaintiff and defendant.
```

### `glossary:respondent:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "respondent" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The respondent is the person a claim is made against in an application, an answer or an appeal. The respondent replies by serving and filing an answer.
```

### `glossary:self-represented-litigant`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "self-represented litigant"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A person running their own case without a lawyer, paralegal or other representative. You are generally allowed to represent yourself, but you are held to the same standard as people with lawyers: you have to learn and follow the court's rules and the law that applies. The judge must be fair to both sides and can explain procedure, but cannot give legal advice.
```

### `glossary:self-represented-litigant:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "self-represented litigant" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A self-represented party who wins can be awarded up to $500 for inconvenience and expense.
```

### `glossary:self-represented-litigant:civil`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "self-represented litigant" (in civil cases in the superior court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Some parties have to be represented by a lawyer, including corporations (unless the court says otherwise) and minors.
```

### `glossary:serve`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "serve"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
To give a court document to another party in a way the rules accept, so they have formal notice of it. Once you serve a document you usually must prove it, most often with an affidavit of service. The first document in a case (the claim or application) has stricter rules than later documents: it must generally be handed over personally or by an approved alternative. Who must be served, how, and by when depends on the document.
```

### `glossary:serve:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "serve" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
You arrange service of your own documents. A plaintiff's claim must be served within six months after it is issued; the court can extend that time.
```

### `glossary:serve:civil`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "serve" (in civil cases in the superior court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
A statement of claim must be served within six months after it is issued. "Deliver" means serve and then file with proof of service.
```

### `glossary:serve:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "serve" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
Family rules use "special service" (the stricter methods, such as handing a copy to the person) and "regular service" (such as mail). An application must be served by special service, by someone other than you, who is at least 18 years old.
```

### `glossary:set-aside`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "set aside"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
To cancel an order, judgment or step so that it no longer has effect. For example, a defendant who was noted in default, or who had default judgment signed against them, can ask the court to set it aside so they can defend the case. You usually ask by motion, and in some cases the other side can agree to it.
```

### `glossary:set-aside:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "set aside" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A motion to set aside default judgment is to be brought as soon as reasonably possible. An order made without notice can be challenged by motion within 30 days after you are served with it.
```

### `glossary:set-aside:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "set aside" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The court can change an order obtained by fraud, containing a mistake, or made without notice.
```

### `glossary:settlement`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "settlement"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
An agreement between the parties that ends a case, avoids it, or narrows what is left to decide. It usually involves paying money or giving up rights, often with a release. You can settle at any time, even during trial. A formal offer to settle that is not accepted is kept from the judge until everything except costs is decided, and it can affect the costs order.
```

### `glossary:settlement:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "settlement" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
Settlements can be written on Terms of Settlement (Form 14D) and filed. Offers can use Form 14A. If a party breaks an accepted offer, the other can ask for judgment on its terms or continue the case.
```

### `glossary:settlement:civil`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "settlement" (in civil cases in the superior court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
The rules on offers to settle say an offer cannot be mentioned in a pleading.
```

### `glossary:settlement:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "settlement" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
Offers can be made even before the case starts, and their terms are kept out of the continuing record.
```

### `glossary:settlement-conference`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "settlement conference"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/areas-of-law/small-claims-court/steps-in-a-case/

```
A private meeting with a judge before trial where the parties talk openly about the case to try to settle it or narrow the issues. The judge may give a view of how the case might be decided. What is said there stays confidential, and a different judge hears the trial. Small Claims and family court both use this name; civil cases have a pre-trial conference instead.
```

### `glossary:settlement-conference:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "settlement conference" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/areas-of-law/small-claims-court/steps-in-a-case/

```
Held in every defended case within 90 days after the first defence is filed, unless the defence admits the whole claim and proposes terms of payment. At least 14 days before, serve and file documents you will rely on and a List of Proposed Witnesses (Form 13A). Not attending or coming unprepared can lead to costs.
```

### `glossary:settlement-conference:civil`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "settlement conference" (in civil cases in the superior court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/areas-of-law/small-claims-court/steps-in-a-case/

```
Not used by this name. The matching step is the pre-trial conference.
```

### `glossary:settlement-conference:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "settlement conference" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/areas-of-law/small-claims-court/steps-in-a-case/

```
Usually comes after a case conference and before trial. Its purposes include settling or narrowing the issues and, if possible, getting a view of how the court might decide.
```

### `glossary:special-party`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "special party"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/990114

```
A family court term for a party, other than a child party, who is, or seems to be, mentally incapable about an issue in the case and as a result needs legal representation. The court can authorize a suitable person to represent them or, if no appropriate person is willing, the Public Guardian and Trustee, with its consent. An offer to settle made or accepted by a special party is not binding on them until the court approves.
```

### `glossary:special-party:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "special party" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/990114

```
Similar situations are covered by "disability", which includes a party who is mentally incapable about an issue in the case, and also minors.
```

### `glossary:special-party:civil`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "special party" (in civil cases in the superior court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/990114

```
Similar situations are covered by "disability", which includes a person who is mentally incapable about an issue in the proceeding, and also minors.
```

### `glossary:spouse`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "spouse"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
In Ontario family law, a spouse is one of two people who are married to each other, including a marriage later found void or voidable if entered in good faith. For support, unmarried partners can also be spouses if they lived together continuously for at least three years, or in a relationship of some permanence and are parents of a child together.
```

### `glossary:statement-of-claim`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "statement of claim"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
The document that starts an action (lawsuit) in the Superior Court of Justice. It names the parties and gives a short summary of the key facts and what you want the court to order. The court issues it, and you then serve it on each defendant. Small Claims Court uses a different form, the plaintiff's claim; family court uses an application.
```

### `glossary:statement-of-claim:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "statement of claim" (in small claims court)

```
The starting document is a Plaintiff's Claim (Form 7A), not a statement of claim.
```

### `glossary:statement-of-claim:civil`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "statement of claim" (in civil cases in the superior court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
Form 14A or 14B. If you need more time, a Notice of Action (Form 14C) gives you thirty more days to file the statement of claim. It must be served within six months after it is issued.
```

### `glossary:statement-of-claim:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "statement of claim" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
A family case starts with an application, not a statement of claim.
```

### `glossary:statute`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "statute"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
A written law passed by the Ontario legislature or the federal Parliament, also called an Act or legislation. A regulation is a more detailed law made under a statute; it usually sets out practical rules and procedures and changes more often. The court rules themselves (Small Claims, civil and family) are regulations.
```

### `glossary:summary-judgment`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "summary judgment"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A final decision on all or part of a case without a full trial, because the court is satisfied there is no genuine issue that needs a trial. A party asks for it by motion, with affidavits or other evidence. The other side cannot rely only on what their documents say; they must show, with evidence, specific facts showing there is a genuine issue for trial. Available in civil and family cases.
```

### `glossary:summary-judgment:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "summary judgment" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The Small Claims rules do not provide for summary judgment motions.
```

### `glossary:summary-judgment:civil`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "summary judgment" (in civil cases in the superior court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Each party must also serve a factum (written legal argument).
```

### `glossary:summary-judgment:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "summary judgment" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Available after an answer is served or the time for it has run out, in any case that does not include a divorce claim.
```

### `glossary:summons-to-witness`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "summons to witness"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
A court document that requires a person to come to court to give evidence, and can also require them to bring documents or things. It is served on the witness with money for attending. A witness who ignores a properly served summons can face serious consequences. Older or general usage calls it a subpoena.
```

### `glossary:summons-to-witness:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "summons to witness" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
Form 18A. Serve it personally at least 10 days before trial, with attendance money (a witness fee and travel expenses). If a properly served witness does not come, the trial judge may issue a warrant for their arrest.
```

### `glossary:summons-to-witness:civil`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "summons to witness" (in civil cases in the superior court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
Form 53A, served on the witness personally with attendance money.
```

### `glossary:summons-to-witness:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "summons to witness" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
Form 23, served by special service with the witness fee at least seven days before the person must be in court or at a questioning. Also used to bring someone to a financial examination.
```

### `glossary:support-deduction-order`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "support deduction order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/96f31

```
An order made along with a support order so that support can be taken directly from money owed to the person who pays support. Their "income source", such as an employer or pension plan, must deduct the support and send it to the Director of the Family Responsibility Office. The court makes it even if no income source is known yet.
```

### `glossary:support-order`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "support order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/96f31

```
A family court order that requires someone to pay support (child support, spousal support or both). It can require regular payments, such as monthly (periodic payments), a lump sum, or other things such as paying certain expenses. When an Ontario court makes a support order, it must also make a support deduction order.
```

### `glossary:territorial-division`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "territorial division"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Used in Small Claims Court for the area a court location serves, such as a county, district or regional municipality, or a listed city such as Ottawa, Toronto or Hamilton. You start your claim in the territorial division where the problem happened or where a defendant lives or does business, or at the court nearest the defendant. If you serve all defendants outside it, you may need an Affidavit for Jurisdiction (Form 11A).
```

### `glossary:timetable`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "timetable"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A schedule with dates for completing the steps needed to move a case forward, such as exchanging documents, examinations and motions.
```

### `glossary:timetable:civil`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "timetable" (in civil cases in the superior court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A timetable is set by a court order or by a written agreement of the parties. If an action may be dismissed for delay and the parties do not agree to a timetable, a party can bring a motion for a status hearing, where the plaintiff must show cause why the action is not to be dismissed for delay.
```

### `glossary:timetable:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "timetable" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Every child protection case follows a timetable set out in the family rules, with a maximum time for each step. The court can lengthen a time only if the best interests of the child require it.
```

### `glossary:transcript`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "transcript"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/access-to-digital-recordings-court-records/accessing-a-digital-recording-ordering-transcripts/

```
A certified written record of what was said at a court hearing, prepared by an authorized court transcriptionist for a fee. Transcripts are used on appeals and some motions, and transcripts of questioning or examinations for discovery can be read into evidence at trial. In the Superior Court of Justice, transcripts of case, settlement and trial management conferences are not available, even to the parties, unless a Superior Court judge orders otherwise.
```

### `glossary:transcript:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "transcript" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/access-to-digital-recordings-court-records/accessing-a-digital-recording-ordering-transcripts/

```
A motion for a new trial needs proof that you have asked for a transcript of the reasons for judgment and any other relevant part. If available, the transcript is served and filed at least three days before the hearing.
```

### `glossary:transcript:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "transcript" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/access-to-digital-recordings-court-records/accessing-a-digital-recording-ordering-transcripts/

```
The trial record includes the relevant parts of any transcript a party intends to rely on at trial.
```

### `glossary:trial`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "trial"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
The final hearing of a case, where the judge hears the witnesses, looks at the evidence and decides the issues the parties could not settle. In civil cases a jury may sometimes decide. Most cases have a conference first to try to settle or narrow the issues; in Small Claims, the judge at the settlement conference will not be the trial judge.
```

### `glossary:trial:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "trial" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
A trial includes a hearing. Trials are scheduled within a trial sitting, a period of time the court sets during which the trial will be held.
```

### `glossary:uncontested-trial`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "uncontested trial"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/990114

```
A family court trial where only the person making the claim gives evidence and makes arguments. It can happen when the other party has not filed an answer, or when their documents were struck out. Evidence is often given by affidavit.
```

### `glossary:valuation-date`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "valuation date"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The date used to value each spouse's property when dividing it under family law. It is the earliest of: the date the spouses separated with no reasonable prospect of living together again; the date of divorce; the date the marriage was declared a nullity; or, if one spouse dies, the day before the death. (A rarer case involves an application about one spouse wasting property.)
```

### `glossary:will`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "will"
- **Source:** https://www.courtsnb-coursnb.ca/content/cour/en/glossary.html

```
A document in which a person directs how their estate (what they own) is to be given out when they die. For estate court steps, it includes any such document for which probate or administration can be granted. See "certificate of appointment of estate trustee".
```

### `glossary:without-notice`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "without notice"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/areas-of-law/small-claims-court/steps-in-a-case/

```
A motion made without first serving the other side, so they are not at the hearing. It is allowed only in limited situations, such as when giving notice is unnecessary or not reasonably possible, or when waiting would cause serious harm. An order made this way must then be served on the people it affects, who can ask the court to set it aside or change it. Also known by the Latin name ex parte.
```

### `glossary:without-notice:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "without notice" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/areas-of-law/small-claims-court/steps-in-a-case/

```
The order must be served on every affected party within five days after it is signed. An affected party can move to set it aside or vary it within 30 days after being served.
```

### `glossary:without-notice:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "without notice" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/areas-of-law/small-claims-court/steps-in-a-case/

```
Allowed, for example, where there is an immediate danger of a child being removed from Ontario, or to a child's or a party's health or safety. The court can later change an order made without notice.
```

### `glossary:without-prejudice`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "without prejudice"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
A label for statements made in a genuine attempt to settle a dispute. If the attempt fails, those statements generally cannot be put before the court as admissions against the person who made them. If they do settle the dispute, they become "with prejudice" and can be used as evidence.
```

### `glossary:witness`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "witness"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
A person who gives evidence in a case under oath or affirmation, in person or by affidavit, because they know something about it. You can be a witness in your own case. A witness may come voluntarily or be required to come by a summons to witness. While testifying, a witness gives facts, not argument.
```

### `glossary:witness:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "witness" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
Witnesses do not attend settlement conferences; you tell the judge what they would say. Each side serves a List of Proposed Witnesses (Form 13A) at least 14 days before the settlement conference.
```

### `glossary:writ-of-seizure-and-sale`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "writ of seizure and sale"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/document/guide-procedures-small-claims-court/after-judgment

```
A court document that lets the enforcement office (sheriff or bailiff) seize and sell the debtor's property to pay a judgment. A writ against land makes it hard for the debtor to sell or mortgage land until the debt is paid. Some personal property, such as clothing and household items up to set amounts, is exempt. In Small Claims and civil cases, once six years have passed since the order, the court's permission (leave) is needed to issue one.
```

### `glossary:writ-of-seizure-and-sale:small-claims`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "writ of seizure and sale" (in small claims court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/document/guide-procedures-small-claims-court/after-judgment

```
There are two writs: personal property (Form 20C), enforced by a bailiff, and land (Form 20D), issued to the sheriff. A writ lasts six years and can be renewed.
```

### `glossary:writ-of-seizure-and-sale:civil`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "writ of seizure and sale" (in civil cases in the superior court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/document/guide-procedures-small-claims-court/after-judgment

```
The writ is Form 60A, issued on a requisition stating the amount owing and the postjudgment interest rate.
```

### `glossary:writ-of-seizure-and-sale:family`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "writ of seizure and sale" (in family court)
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/document/guide-procedures-small-claims-court/after-judgment

```
The writ is Form 28, issued when a recipient files a request (Form 28A) and a statement of money owed.
```

### `glossary:amicus-curiae`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "amicus curiae"
- **Source:** https://www.fct-cf.ca/en/pages/representing-yourself/glossary

```
Latin for "friend of the court": a person, usually a lawyer, who helps the court understand the issues without acting for either side. The court usually asks for one.
```

### `glossary:de-novo`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "de novo"
- **Source:** https://www.courtsnb-coursnb.ca/content/cour/en/glossary.html

```
Latin for "anew". A trial or hearing de novo is the matter heard again, a second time.
```

### `glossary:ex-parte`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "ex parte"
- **Source:** https://www.fct-cf.ca/en/pages/representing-yourself/glossary

```
Latin for a court step taken with only one side present, without the other side being told first. Ontario's court rules use the phrase "without notice" instead (for example, a motion without notice). See "without notice".
```

### `glossary:in-camera`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "in camera"
- **Source:** https://www.fct-cf.ca/en/pages/representing-yourself/glossary

```
A hearing, or part of one, held in private with the public kept out. The public generally cannot get the recordings or records of the parts heard in camera.
```

### `glossary:nunc-pro-tunc`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "nunc pro tunc"
- **Source:** https://www.fct-cf.ca/en/pages/representing-yourself/glossary

```
Describes an order or step the court makes now but that takes effect as if it had been made at an earlier date.
```

### `glossary:prima-facie`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "prima facie"
- **Source:** https://www.manitobacourts.mb.ca/general-information/definitions-understanding-legal-words/

```
Latin for "at first sight". Describes a fact that is taken as true unless evidence shows otherwise.
```

### `glossary:pro-bono`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "pro bono"
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/guides-and-service-resources/guide-to-representing-yourself/civil-resources-to-help-self-represented-litigants/steps-to-civil-case/

```
Legal services given free of charge. The Latin means "for the good".
```

### `glossary:stare-decisis`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "stare decisis"
- **Source:** https://www.manitobacourts.mb.ca/general-information/definitions-understanding-legal-words/

```
The rule that judges follow earlier binding decisions of their own court or a higher court. It is why a decision from a higher court binds lower courts in later cases. See "precedent".
```

### `glossary:viva-voce`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / glossary
- **Appears in:** Glossary, "viva voce"
- **Source:** https://www.courtsnb-coursnb.ca/content/cour/en/glossary.html

```
Spoken aloud. Viva voce evidence is what a witness says in court, as opposed to evidence given in writing in an affidavit.
```

## form-guidance (430)

### `form-guide:small-claims:1A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 1A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Used to list the remaining parties to a case when a court form does not have enough space for all of them on the first page. It is attached right after that first page.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:1A.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 1A.1; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Lists the remaining debtors when a certificate of judgment, a writ of seizure and sale of personal property or of land, or a direction to enforce a writ of seizure and sale of personal property lacks space for all of them. It is attached to that form.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:1B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 1B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Used by a party to ask to change how the party, their representative or a witness attends a step. The request sets out the party's reasons and is served and filed, with proof of service, at least 30 days before the hearing date.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:1C`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 1C; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Used by a party to object to a request to change how someone attends a step. It is served and filed, with proof of service, no later than seven days after being served with the request.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:4A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 4A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Filled in by a person acting as litigation guardian for someone under a disability. It states the nature of the disability, the guardian's relationship to that person, and that the guardian has no interest in the case against that person's interest.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:4B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 4B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
The affidavit (sworn statement) supporting a motion for an order about money payable to a person under disability under an order or settlement, such as an order paying it out of court. It is used instead of an affidavit in Form 15A.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:5A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 5A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Served with the claim by a plaintiff suing a partnership under its firm name, when the plaintiff wants an order that could be enforced personally against someone as a partner.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:7A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 7A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
The form used to start a case. A plaintiff files it with the clerk, with a copy for each defendant, and it is served personally or by an alternative to personal service.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:8A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 8A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A sworn statement by the person who served a document, used to prove that the document was served.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:8B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 8B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Used by a lawyer or paralegal to prove service of a document that they served or caused to be served, when they are satisfied the service was done.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:9A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 9A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
The form a defendant uses to dispute a plaintiff's claim. A defendant who disputes the claim serves it on every other party and files it, with proof of service, within 20 days of being served with the claim.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:9B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 9B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A request to the clerk, used for things such as asking to note a defendant in default, asking for an assessment hearing, or disputing a proposal by asking for a terms of payment hearing.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:10A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 10A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A defendant's claim against the plaintiff, or against another person where it arises out of the transaction or occurrence the plaintiff relies on or relates to the plaintiff's claim. It may be issued within 20 days after the defence is filed, or later, before trial or default judgment, with leave.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:11A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 11A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A sworn statement filed with the clerk to prove a case was properly brought in that court's area when all defendants were served outside it. The clerk needs this proof before noting any defendant in default.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:11B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 11B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
The judgment the clerk may sign against a defendant who has been noted in default, for a debt or a set amount of money, including interest if claimed. The clerk serves it on all parties by mail or email.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:11.2A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 11.2A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Asks the clerk for an order on consent granting certain kinds of relief listed in the rules, such as setting aside a noting in default or dismissing an action. The request is signed by all parties. If refused, the clerk serves the request on all parties with reasons.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:11.3A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 11.3A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Used by a plaintiff to discontinue (drop) their claim against a defendant who did not file a defence in time. The plaintiff serves it on all defendants who were served with the claim and files it with proof of service.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:13A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 13A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A list of the witnesses a party plans to call and other people who know about the matters in dispute. Each party serves and files it at least 14 days before the date of the settlement conference.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:13B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 13B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A consent of the parties, used for example to allow matters discussed at a settlement or trial management conference to be disclosed, or, where the amount in dispute is under the appealable limit, signed by all parties so a judge may order final judgment at the settlement conference.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:14A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 14A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A form that may be used to make an offer to settle a case.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:14B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 14B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A form that may be used to accept an offer to settle.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:14C`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 14C; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A form that may be used to withdraw an offer to settle.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:14D`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 14D; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Used to set out the terms of an offer to settle that has been accepted.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:15A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 15A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
The form used to bring a motion, combining the notice of motion and a supporting affidavit (sworn statement). A plaintiff may also use it to ask for a motion in writing for an assessment of damages.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:15B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 15B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A general affidavit form for use where the rules permit or require an affidavit and no other form is specified. A responding affidavit on a motion is served on every party who filed a claim or defence and filed, with proof of service, at least two days before the hearing.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:18A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 18A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Used by a party to require a person in Ontario to come to a trial as a witness. It is served personally at least 10 days before the trial date, with attendance money paid or offered to the witness.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:18B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 18B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A warrant a trial judge may issue to all police officers in Ontario to apprehend a witness and bring the witness before the court, when a witness whose evidence is material fails to attend or remain at the trial as required by a summons to witness served on the witness.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:20A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 20A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Issued by the clerk, at the creditor's request, to the clerk at the court location the creditor names, when there is default under an order to pay money. The request is supported by an affidavit stating the amount still owing.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:20B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 20B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Used to enforce an order to deliver personal property. The clerk issues it to a bailiff at the request of the person the order favours, with an affidavit stating the property has not been delivered.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:20C`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 20C; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Issued by the clerk to a bailiff at the creditor's request if there is default under an order for the payment or recovery of money, supported by an affidavit (Form 20P) stating the amount still owing. More than six years after the order, leave of the court is required.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:20D`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 20D; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Used to enforce an order to pay money through the seizure and sale of land. The clerk issues it to the sheriff at the creditor's request, supported by an affidavit stating the amount still owing.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:20E`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 20E; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Issued by the clerk, naming a garnishee, after the creditor files an affidavit (Form 20P). Leave is needed if more than six years have passed since the order or enforcement is subject to a condition. Served with Form 20P on the debtor and Form 20F on the garnishee.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:20E.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 20E.1; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Used to renew a notice of garnishment before it expires. It is filed with the clerk of the court that issued the notice of garnishment, together with an affidavit for enforcement request.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:20F`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 20F; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A statement a garnishee files with the court setting out the particulars. The rules say certain garnishees file it within 10 days after service of the notice of garnishment.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:20G`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 20G; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Sent by a creditor to any co-owners of a debt, with a copy of the garnishee's statement, after the creditor is served with that statement.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:20H`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 20H; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
Issued by the clerk at a creditor's request, when there is default under an order to pay money, directed to the debtor or another person to be examined. The creditor serves it personally or by an alternative to personal service.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:20I`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 20I; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/980258

```
A form an individual debtor completes for an examination, serving it on the creditor but not filing it with the court, and giving a copy to the judge. The clerk also serves it on an individual defendant with a notice of hearing.
```

### `form-guide:small-claims:20J`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 20J; the case forms page card for the same form

```

- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 28A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

A crossclaim, included in the same document as the statement of defence, which is titled a statement of defence and crossclaim.
```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 28B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The defence to a crossclaim, one of the pleadings in a crossclaim.
```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 28C; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A reply to a defence to crossclaim, if there is one. The rule says it is delivered within ten days after service of the defence to crossclaim.
```

- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 29A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

The form used for a third party claim, including a fourth or later party claim or a claim by a defendant to a counterclaim or crossclaim.
```

### `form-guide:civil:29B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 29B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

The defence a third party delivers to defend against a third party claim. It is also used for a defence by a fourth or later party.
```

- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 29C; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

A reply to a third party defence, if there is one. The rule says it is delivered within ten days after service of the third party defence.
```

```

### `form-guide:civil:30B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 30B; the case forms page card for the same form

An affidavit of documents made by a corporation or partnership and served on every other party. It discloses all documents relevant to any matter in issue in the action that are or have been in the party's possession, control or power.
```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 30C; the case forms page card for the same form

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 34B; the case forms page card for the same form

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms

```

### `form-guide:civil:34D`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 34D; the case forms page card for the same form

```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 34E; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 35A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 35B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 37A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 37B; the case forms page card for the same form

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 37C; the case forms page card for the same form

```

### `form-guide:civil:38B`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 38B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A confirmation of application that a party making an application on notice gives the registrar before the hearing, by email or at the court office, with a copy emailed to the other party. A corrected one is given if it is no longer correct.
```

### `form-guide:civil:42A`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 42A; the case forms page card for the same form

```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 43A; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 44A; the case forms page card for the same form

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 47A; the case forms page card for the same form

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms

- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms

- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 55E; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 55F; the case forms page card for the same form

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 55G; the case forms page card for the same form

- **Status:** draft

- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 59B; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 59C; the case forms page card for the same form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The form used for an order on appeal.
```

### `form-guide:civil:59D`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms
- **Appears in:** Forms guide, Form 59D; the case forms page card for the same form

- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms

- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms

- **Pathway / stage:** civil / forms

- **Status:** draft

Why: The court needs proof of service before a case can move forward without a response.
```

### `sc-defence-filed`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / substance
- **Appears in:** Guided intake and the Small Claims static form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/docs/980258_e.doc

```
Has the other party filed a Defence with the court?

Why: A defendant generally has 20 calendar days to serve and file a defence. If that time has passed with no defence filed, the plaintiff may be able to ask the clerk to note the defendant in default (a request in Form 9B, with proof the claim was served).
```

### `sc-defence-time-elapsed`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / substance
- **Appears in:** Guided intake and the Small Claims static form
- **Source:** https://www.ontariocourts.ca/scj/areas-of-law/small-claims-court/default-proceedings/

```
Has it been 20 calendar days since the defendant was served with the claim?

Why: This helps identify the procedural stage after service when no Defence has been recorded.
```

### `sc-defendant-noted-in-default`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / substance
- **Appears in:** Guided intake and the Small Claims static form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/docs/980258_e.doc

```
If the defendant hasn't filed a Defence: what date were they served, and how was the claim served on them? And have you already asked the clerk to note them in default?

Why: A defendant who wants to dispute a claim has 20 days from being served to serve and file a Defence. How that period is counted is set by the Rules: the first day is excluded and the last day is included, and if the last day falls on a holiday the period ends on the next day that is not a holiday -- and "holiday" is defined to include any Saturday or Sunday. So weekends in the middle are counted and extend nothing; only the last day moves. When service counts as effective depends on how it was done. For personal service, the Rules do not state a separate effective day; the affidavit of service records when it was done. Where a copy is left with an adult member of the household and another copy is mailed or couriered, it is the fifth day after mailing or verified courier delivery. Where a claim is sent to an individual's home by registered mail or courier and a signature verifying receipt is obtained, the Rules make service effective on the date that signature shows receipt -- not the date of mailing. (The separate five-day rule for documents sent by mail or courier expressly does NOT apply to a claim served that way.) One thing the Rules do not say: how those service-effectiveness provisions interact with the counting rule -- whether the effective day is the excluded first day, for instance. Because the regulation is silent on that, this site does not calculate the date for you. These are the facts to confirm so you can work it out, and the court or a licensed paralegal or lawyer can confirm it.
```

### `sc-defendant-service-method`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / substance
- **Appears in:** Guided intake and the Small Claims static form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/docs/980258_e.doc

```
How and when was the Plaintiff's Claim delivered to you (for example, handed to you in person, left with someone else, or sent by registered mail, courier or email)?

Why: A defendant who wants to dispute a claim has 20 days from being served to serve and file a Defence. When service counts as effective depends on how it was done: in person, it is the day it happened; where a copy is left with an adult member of the household and another copy is mailed or couriered, it is the fifth day after mailing or verified courier delivery; where a claim is sent to an individual's home by registered mail or courier and a signature verifying receipt is obtained, the Rules make service effective on the date that signature shows receipt, not the date of mailing. (The separate five-day rule for documents sent by mail or courier expressly does NOT apply to a claim served that way.) The Rules also count a period by excluding the first day and including the last, and if the last day falls on a holiday the period ends on the next day that is not a holiday -- with "holiday" defined to include any Saturday or Sunday, so weekends in between are counted and extend nothing. What the Rules do NOT say is how those two things interact -- whether the effective day is the excluded first day, for instance. Because the regulation is silent on that, this site does not calculate the date for you. These are the facts to write down so you can work it out, and the court or a licensed paralegal or lawyer can confirm it.
```

### `sc-defendant-counterclaim`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / substance
- **Appears in:** Guided intake and the Small Claims static form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/docs/980258_e.doc

```
Do you believe the plaintiff, or someone else, owes you money or is responsible for part of what happened? (If you have already started your own claim about it, say so.)

Why: A defendant can bring their own claim against the plaintiff, or against someone else where it arises out of the same transaction or occurrence or relates to the plaintiff's claim, as part of the same case, called a Defendant's Claim (Form 10A). The Rules say it may be ISSUED within 20 days after the day the defence is filed -- issuing and filing are different steps, and the 20 days runs from the day the defence was filed, not from when it was served or received. Missing that window does not end it: after those 20 days a Defendant's Claim may still be issued with leave of the court, at any point before trial or default judgment. After trial or default judgment that route is no longer available. Once issued it still has to be served on every person it is made against. Whether any of that fits your situation is yours to decide -- this question only records what you think happened and what you have done so far.
```

### `sc-defendant-admission-payment`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / substance
- **Appears in:** Guided intake and the Small Claims static form
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/docs/980258_e.doc

```
Is there any part of this claim you accept you owe? (If so, say whether the difficulty is the amount itself or paying it all at once.)

Why: The Rules provide a route for this. A defendant who admits liability for all or part of the plaintiff's claim but wants to arrange terms of payment may, IN THE DEFENCE, admit liability and propose terms of payment. What happens next depends on the plaintiff. If the plaintiff does not dispute the proposal within 20 days after service of the defence, the defendant must then make payment in accordance with the proposal AS IF IT WERE A COURT ORDER -- and if they do not, the plaintiff can serve a notice of default of payment (Form 20L), and the clerk signs judgment for the unpaid balance of the undisputed amount when the plaintiff files an affidavit of default of payment (Form 20M) swearing, among other things, that 15 days have passed since that notice was served. If the plaintiff does dispute it, they file and serve a request to clerk (Form 9B) for a terms of payment hearing, and the clerk fixes a time and serves notice of the hearing. Whether to admit any part of a claim is a significant decision and entirely yours. This question only records what you tell us.
```

### `next:small-claims:starting-case`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / starting-case
- **Appears in:** Case summary and generated documents
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/docs/980258_e.doc

```
An action is started by filing a Plaintiff's Claim (Form 7A) with the clerk, together with a copy for each defendant. A copy for each defendant is not required if the claim is filed electronically (r. 7.01 (1), (1.1)).

The claim must be served on the defendant within six months after the date it is issued. The court may extend that time, before or after the six months has passed (r. 8.01 (2)).

Service is proved by an Affidavit of Service (Form 8A), or by a lawyer or paralegal's Certificate of Service (Form 8B) where that licensee served it, or caused it to be served, and is satisfied service was effected (r. 8.09.1).
```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / responding
- **Appears in:** Case summary and generated documents
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/docs/980258_e.doc

```
A defendant who wishes to dispute a claim must, within 20 days of being served, serve a Defence (Form 9A) on every other party and file it with the clerk, with proof of service (r. 9.01).

Proof of service is an Affidavit of Service (Form 8A) or a lawyer or paralegal's Certificate of Service (Form 8B) (r. 8.09.1).
```

If no defence has been filed in time, the plaintiff may ask the clerk to note the defendant in default. The clerk requires a request to note in default (which may be made in Form 9B) and proof that the claim was served within the court's territorial division (r. 11.01 (1)).

If every defendant was served outside that territorial division, no defendant can be noted in default until an Affidavit for Jurisdiction (Form 11A) is filed with the clerk, or the point is proved before a judge (r. 11.01 (3)).
```

A List of Proposed Witnesses (Form 13A) must also be served on every other party and filed with the court at least 14 days before the settlement conference (r. 13.03 (2)).

A document, written statement or audio or visual record served on all parties who were served with the notice of trial, at least 30 days before the trial date, will be received in evidence unless the trial judge orders otherwise (r. 18.02 (1)). The party serving it must include the name, telephone number and address for service of the witness or author (r. 18.02 (3)).

Service of a summons to witness, and the payment or tender of attendance money, may be proved by an Affidavit of Service (Form 8A) or a lawyer or paralegal's Certificate of Service (Form 8B) (r. 18.03 (4)).

### `next:small-claims:enforcement`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / enforcement
- **Appears in:** Case summary and generated documents
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/docs/980258_e.doc

```
An order for the payment or recovery of money may be enforced by a writ of seizure and sale of personal property (Form 20C) under rule 20.06, a writ of seizure and sale of land (Form 20D) under rule 20.07, and garnishment under rule 20.08, and a further order as to payment may be made after an examination (r. 20.03).

If there is default under the order, the clerk of a court in the territorial division where the debtor lives or carries on business will, at the creditor's request, issue a notice of examination (Form 20H), supported by an affidavit for enforcement request (Form 20P) and, if the order was made in another territorial division, a certificate of judgment (Form 20A) (r. 20.10 (1), (2)).

To enforce at another court location, the clerk will, at the creditor's request supported by Form 20P stating the amount still owing, issue a certificate of judgment (Form 20A) to the clerk at that location (r. 20.04 (1)).

The court may stay enforcement, and may vary the times and proportions in which money is to be paid if it is satisfied that the debtor's circumstances have changed (r. 20.02 (1)).
```

### `next:small-claims:urgent`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / urgent
- **Appears in:** Case summary and generated documents
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/docs/980258_e.doc

```
The court may lengthen or shorten any time set by the rules or by an order, on such terms as are just (r. 3.02 (1)). A time for serving or filing a document can also be lengthened or shortened by filing the consent of the parties (r. 3.02 (2)).

A party who has been noted in default, or has a default judgment against them, can make a motion to set it aside. Under rule 11.06, the court may do so if it is satisfied of two things: that the party has a defence on the merits and a reasonable explanation for the default, and that the motion is made as soon as is reasonably possible.

A motion is made by a notice of motion and supporting affidavit (Form 15A), with a hearing date obtained from the clerk before it is served (r. 15.01 (1), (2)).
```

If you are not sure what stage your case is at, that is a question a lawyer or paralegal can help with. Ontario's Small Claims Court guide says that if you wish to consult an Ontario lawyer or paralegal, you may contact the Law Society Referral Service, operated by the Law Society of Ontario. It can give you the name of a lawyer or paralegal in your area, who will provide a free initial consultation of up to 30 minutes to help determine your rights and options.

You can ask for a referral by completing the online request form at www.lawsocietyreferralservice.ca.
