```
Documentary discovery and the affidavit of documents
```

### `guide:discovery:3.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Documentary discovery and the affidavit of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
For these rules, “document” includes “a sound recording, videotape, film, photograph, chart, graph, map, plan, survey, book of account, and data and information in electronic form”. “Every document relevant to any matter in issue in an action that is or has been in the possession, control or power of a party to the action shall be disclosed”, “whether or not privilege is claimed in respect of the document.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 30.01 (1) (a), 30.02 (1))
```

### `guide:discovery:3.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Documentary discovery and the affidavit of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A party “shall serve on every other party an affidavit of documents (Form 30A or 30B)”. It lists, in separate schedules, relevant documents the party does not object to producing, documents for which the party claims privilege “and the grounds for the claim”, and documents no longer in the party's possession, control or power, with a statement of when and how that happened and their present location. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 30.03 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:discovery:3.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Documentary discovery and the affidavit of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A party who serves a request to inspect documents (Form 30C) “is entitled to inspect any document that is not privileged and that is referred to in the other party's affidavit of documents”. The party served names a date “within five days after the service of the request”. “An affidavit of documents shall not be filed unless it is relevant to an issue on a pending motion or at trial.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 30.03 (5), 30.04 (1), (3))
```

### `guide:discovery:3.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Documentary discovery and the affidavit of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
If a party later obtains a relevant non-privileged document, or finds the affidavit inaccurate or incomplete, “the party shall forthwith serve a supplementary affidavit”. Disclosing or producing a document “shall not be taken as an admission of its relevance or admissibility.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 30.05, 30.07)
```

### `guide:discovery:4:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Privilege and failing to disclose
```

### `guide:discovery:4.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Privilege and failing to disclose"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Relevant documents must be produced for inspection if requested, “unless privilege is claimed in respect of the document.” “Where privilege is claimed for a document, the court may inspect the document to determine the validity of the claim.” Rule 30 does not explain what privilege is, and this site does not yet have a source that does. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 30.02 (2), 30.04 (6))
```

### `guide:discovery:4.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Privilege and failing to disclose"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A party that claims privilege for a document and does not abandon the claim, by giving notice in writing and providing a copy of the document or producing it for inspection, “at least 90 days before the commencement of the trial”, “may not use the document at the trial, except to impeach the testimony of a witness or with leave of the trial judge.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 30.09)
```

### `guide:discovery:4.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Privilege and failing to disclose"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
If a party fails to disclose a document in an affidavit of documents or supplementary affidavit, or fails to produce it as required by the rules, a court order or an undertaking, then if the document is favourable to the party's case, “the party may not use the document at the trial, except with leave of the trial judge”. If it is not favourable, “the court may make such order as is just.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 30.08 (1))
```

### `guide:discovery:4.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Privilege and failing to disclose"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
If a party fails to serve an affidavit of documents, fails to produce a document for inspection as the rules require, or fails to comply with an order under rules 30.02 to 30.11, the court may, among other things, “dismiss the action, if the party is a plaintiff, or strike out the statement of defence, if the party is a defendant”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 30.08 (2))
```

### `guide:discovery:4.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Privilege and failing to disclose"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
On a motion by a party, the court may order a non-party to produce a non-privileged document for inspection where it is satisfied that “the document is relevant to a material issue in the action” and “it would be unfair to require the moving party to proceed to trial without having discovery of the document.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 30.10 (1))
```

### `guide:discovery:5:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Examination for discovery: who, when and how long
```

### `guide:discovery:5.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination for discovery: who, when and how long"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
An examination for discovery “may take the form of an oral examination or, at the option of the examining party, an examination by written questions and answers”, but not both without leave. Where more than one party is entitled to examine a person, the examination is oral “unless all the parties entitled to examine the person agree otherwise.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 31.02 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:discovery:5.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination for discovery: who, when and how long"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A party “may examine for discovery any other party adverse in interest, once”, and more than once only with leave of the court. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 31.03 (1))
```

### `guide:discovery:5.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination for discovery: who, when and how long"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A party may examine more than one person only as subrules 31.03 (2) to (8) permit. For example, where a corporation may be examined, the examining party may examine any officer, director or employee on its behalf, but more than one “only with the consent of the parties or the leave of the court.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 31.03 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:discovery:5.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination for discovery: who, when and how long"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A party who seeks to examine a plaintiff may serve a notice of examination or written questions “only after delivering a statement of defence and, unless the parties agree otherwise, serving an affidavit of documents.” A defendant may be examined after delivering a defence (with the examining party's affidavit of documents served, unless agreed otherwise) or after being noted in default. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 31.04 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:discovery:5.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination for discovery: who, when and how long"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
“No party shall, in conducting oral examinations for discovery, exceed a total of seven hours of examination, regardless of the number of parties or other persons to be examined, except with the consent of the parties or with leave of the court.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 31.05.1 (1))
```

### `guide:discovery:5.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination for discovery: who, when and how long"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
In an action under the simplified procedure (Rule 76), “no party shall, in conducting oral examinations for discovery in relation to an action proceeding under this Rule, exceed a total of three hours of examination, regardless of the number of parties or other persons to be examined.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 76.04 (2))
```

### `guide:discovery:6:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Examination for discovery: scope and answers
```

### `guide:discovery:6.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination for discovery: scope and answers"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A person examined “shall answer, to the best of his or her knowledge, information and belief, any proper question relevant to any matter in issue in the action”. A question may not be objected to on the ground that “the information sought is evidence”. A party may also obtain “the names and addresses of persons who might reasonably be expected to have knowledge of transactions or occurrences in issue in the action, unless the court orders otherwise.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 31.06 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:discovery:6.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination for discovery: scope and answers"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A party, or a person examined on behalf of or in place of a party, fails to answer if they refuse, or if a question taken under advisement or an undertaking is not answered “within 60 days after the response.” The party then “may not introduce at the trial the information that was not provided, except with leave of the trial judge.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 31.07 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:discovery:6.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination for discovery: scope and answers"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
If a party later finds an answer “was incorrect or incomplete when made” or “is no longer correct and complete”, “the party shall forthwith provide the information in writing to every other party.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 31.09 (1))
```

### `guide:discovery:6.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination for discovery: scope and answers"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The court may grant leave to examine for discovery a person “who there is reason to believe has information relevant to a material issue in the action”, other than an expert engaged by or for a party in preparation for contemplated or pending litigation. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 31.10 (1))
```

### `guide:discovery:6.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination for discovery: scope and answers"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Leave is granted only if the court is satisfied that the moving party could not obtain the information from persons it is entitled to examine or from that person, that it would be unfair to proceed to trial without examining the person, and that the examination will not unduly delay the trial, entail unreasonable expense for other parties or be unfair to the person. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 31.10 (2))
```

### `guide:discovery:7:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
How oral examinations are conducted
```

### `guide:discovery:7.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "How oral examinations are conducted"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Where a party acts in person, a notice of examination (Form 34A) is served on the party “personally or by an alternative to personal service.” A person to be examined who resides in Ontario “shall be given not less than two days notice of the time and place of the examination, unless the court orders otherwise.” Every other party is also given not less than two days notice. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 34.04 (1), 34.05 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:discovery:7.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "How oral examinations are conducted"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The person examined “shall take an oath or make an affirmation”. They produce the non-privileged documents rule 30.04 (4) requires, and those the notice of examination requires. Where a question is objected to, “the objector shall state briefly the reason for the objection, and the question and the brief statement shall be recorded.” A ruling may be obtained on motion. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 34.08 (1), 34.10 (2), 34.12 (1), (3))
```

### `guide:discovery:7.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "How oral examinations are conducted"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
An examination may be adjourned to seek directions where, for example, it “is being conducted in bad faith, or in an unreasonable manner so as to annoy, embarrass or oppress the person being examined”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 34.14 (1))
```

### `guide:discovery:7.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "How oral examinations are conducted"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
If a person fails to attend, or refuses to answer a proper question or produce a required document, the court may, among other things, order the person to reattend and answer where an objection is held to be improper, and, where the person is a party or is examined on a party's behalf, “dismiss the party's proceeding or strike out the party's defence”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 34.15 (1))
```

### `guide:discovery:7.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "How oral examinations are conducted"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
“Every examination shall be recorded in its entirety in question and answer form in a manner that permits the preparation of a typed transcript”, unless ordered or agreed otherwise. On request, a typed transcript is to be completed “within four weeks after receipt of the request.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 34.16, 34.17 (1))
```

### `guide:discovery:8:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Examination by written questions
```

### `guide:discovery:8.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination by written questions"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A written examination is conducted “by serving a list of the questions to be answered (Form 35A) on the person to be examined and every other party.” The questions are answered by affidavit (Form 35B), served on the examining party “within fifteen days after service of the list of questions.” An objection is made in the affidavit “with a brief statement of the reason for the objection.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 35.01, 35.02 (1), 35.03)
```

### `guide:discovery:8.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination by written questions"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
If the examining party is not satisfied with an answer, it may, “within ten days after receiving the answer, serve a further list of written questions which shall be answered within fifteen days after service.” If answers are “evasive, unresponsive or otherwise unsatisfactory”, the court may order an oral examination. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 35.04 (1), (3))
```

### `guide:discovery:8.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Discovery in a civil action, "Examination by written questions"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
“Examination for discovery by written questions and answers under Rule 35” is “not permitted in an action under this Rule”, meaning an action under the simplified procedure. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 76.04 (1))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:title`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Mandatory mediation in civil actions
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:intro`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
This guide explains what Rule 24.1 of the Rules of Civil Procedure says about mandatory mediation in some Superior Court of Justice actions: where it applies, when the session happens, choosing a mediator, attendance, documents, and what happens afterwards.
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:1:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
What mandatory mediation is
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:1.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "What mandatory mediation is"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Rule 24.1 “provides for mandatory mediation in specified actions, in order to reduce cost and delay in litigation and facilitate the early and fair resolution of disputes.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.01)
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:1.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "What mandatory mediation is"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
“In mediation, a neutral third party facilitates communication among the parties to a dispute, to assist them in reaching a mutually acceptable resolution.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.02)
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:1.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "What mandatory mediation is"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
In this Rule, a “defence” means “a notice of intent to defend”, “a statement of defence”, or a notice of motion in response to an action, other than a motion challenging the court's jurisdiction. Several time limits in this Rule run from the first defence filed. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.03, 24.1.09 (1), (6))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:2:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Where it applies
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:2.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "Where it applies"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The Rule applies to actions governed by it immediately before January 1, 2010, and to actions commenced on or after January 1, 2010 in “The City of Ottawa.”, “The City of Toronto.” or “The County of Essex.” It also applies to actions transferred to one of those counties on or after January 1, 2014, unless the court orders otherwise. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.04 (1))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:2.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "Where it applies"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The Rule does not apply to some actions, including “actions under Rule 64 (Mortgage Actions)”, actions on the Toronto Region Commercial List, actions under the Construction Act (except trust claims), and actions under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (Canada). It does not apply to actions certified as class proceedings, and applies to an action started under the Class Proceedings Act, 1992 “only if certification as a class proceeding has been denied”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.04 (2), (2.1))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:2.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "Where it applies"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
“The court may make an order on a party's motion exempting the action from this Rule.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.05)
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:3:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
When the session happens
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:3.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "When the session happens"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
“A mediation session shall take place within 180 days after the first defence has been filed, unless the court orders otherwise.” In deciding whether to extend or shorten that time, the court considers all the circumstances, including the number of parties, the state of the pleadings, the complexity of the issues, and whether a party intends to bring a summary judgment motion. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.09 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:3.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "When the session happens"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
For an action transferred to Ottawa, Toronto or Essex on or after January 1, 2014, the 180-day time limit and the automatic assignment of a mediator after 180 days do not apply, and “the court may make an order, on motion or otherwise, specifying the date by which a mediation session must take place.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.09 (2.1))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:3.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "When the session happens"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The session “may be postponed to a later date if, (a) the parties consent to the date in writing; and (b) the consent is filed with the mediation co-ordinator.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.09 (3))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:4:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The mediator
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:4.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "The mediator"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The mediation is conducted by “a person chosen by the agreement of the parties from the list for a county”, a person assigned from the list by the mediation co-ordinator, or “a person who is not named on a list, if the parties consent.” “The parties shall choose a mediator under subrule 24.1.08 (2).” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.08 (2), 24.1.09 (4))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:4.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "The mediator"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Before the action is set down for trial, one of the parties files with the mediation co-ordinator a notice (Form 24.1A) “stating the mediator's name and the date of the mediation session”, or a mediator's report showing the mediation has concluded. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.09 (5))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:4.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "The mediator"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
If the co-ordinator receives none of the listed documents or orders within 180 days after the first defence is filed, the co-ordinator “shall immediately assign a mediator from the list, unless the court orders otherwise.” The assigned mediator serves a notice (Form 24.1B) at least 20 days before the session, “advising that attendance is obligatory.” The date is to be “within 90 days after the appointment of the mediator, unless the court orders otherwise.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.09 (6), (7), (7.1))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:5:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Documents before the session
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:5.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "Documents before the session"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
“At least seven days before the mediation session, every party shall prepare a statement in Form 24.1C and provide a copy to every other party and to the mediator.” The statement “shall identify the factual and legal issues in dispute and briefly set out the position and interests of the party making the statement.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.10 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:5.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "Documents before the session"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The party making the statement “shall attach to it any documents that the party considers of central importance in the action.” “The plaintiff shall include a copy of the pleadings with the copy of the statement that is provided to the mediator.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.10 (3), (4))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:6:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Attendance and confidentiality
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:6.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "Attendance and confidentiality"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
“The parties, and their lawyers if the parties are represented, are required to attend the mediation session unless the court orders otherwise.” A party who needs another person's approval to settle arranges, before the mediation session, “to have ready telephone access to the other person throughout the session”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.11 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:6.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "Attendance and confidentiality"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Unless the court orders otherwise, where an insurer may be liable to satisfy all or part of a judgment in the action, or to indemnify or reimburse an insured party for money paid under it, a representative of the insurer attends, and the insured party is not required to. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.11 (1.1))
```

### `guide:mandatory-mediation:6.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Mandatory mediation in civil actions, "Attendance and confidentiality"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194


- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
This guide explains what the court rules say about deciding a case, or part of one, without a full trial (summary judgment) in civil and family cases, and about the simplified procedure for some civil actions in the Superior Court of Justice.
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:1:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Civil summary judgment: who can ask, and when
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:1.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Civil summary judgment: who can ask, and when"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A plaintiff may, “after the defendant has delivered a statement of defence or served a notice of motion, move with supporting affidavit material or other evidence for summary judgment on all or part of the claim in the statement of claim.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 20.01 (1))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:1.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Civil summary judgment: who can ask, and when"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A defendant may, “after delivering a statement of defence, move with supporting affidavit material or other evidence for summary judgment dismissing all or part of the claim in the statement of claim.” A plaintiff may also ask, without notice, for leave to serve the motion with the statement of claim, which “may be given where special urgency is shown”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 20.01 (2), (3))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:2:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Civil summary judgment: evidence and factums
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:2.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Civil summary judgment: evidence and factums"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
A responding party “may not rest solely on the allegations or denials in the party's pleadings, but must set out, in affidavit material or other evidence, specific facts showing that there is a genuine issue requiring a trial.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 20.02 (2))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:2.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Civil summary judgment: evidence and factums"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
An affidavit may be made on information and belief, but on the hearing of the motion the court may, if appropriate, “draw an adverse inference from the failure of a party to provide the evidence of any person having personal knowledge of contested facts.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 20.02 (1))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:2.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Civil summary judgment: evidence and factums"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Each party serves a factum. The moving party's factum is served and filed “at least seven days before the hearing”, and the responding party's “at least four days before the hearing.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 20.03 (1), (2), (3))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:3:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Civil summary judgment: how the court decides
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:3.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Civil summary judgment: how the court decides"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The court “shall grant summary judgment if” it “is satisfied that there is no genuine issue requiring a trial with respect to a claim or defence”, or the parties agree to have all or part of the claim decided this way and the court is satisfied that it is appropriate. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 20.04 (2))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:3.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Civil summary judgment: how the court decides"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
In deciding whether there is a genuine issue requiring a trial, a judge may weigh the evidence, evaluate the credibility of a deponent, and draw any reasonable inference from the evidence, “unless it is in the interest of justice for such powers to be exercised only at a trial”. A judge may also order that oral evidence be presented. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 20.04 (2.1), (2.2))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:3.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Civil summary judgment: how the court decides"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
If the only genuine issue is the amount, the court “may order a trial of that issue or grant judgment with a reference to determine the amount.” If the only genuine issue is a question of law, the court may decide it and grant judgment, but a motion made to an associate judge is adjourned to be heard by a judge. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 20.04 (3), (4))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:4:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Civil summary judgment: if a trial is still needed, and costs"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Where summary judgment is refused or granted only in part, the court may specify “what material facts are not in dispute” and define the issues to be tried, and order that the action proceed to trial expeditiously. It may also give directions, such as time limits for motions or a discovery plan. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 20.05 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:4.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Civil summary judgment: if a trial is still needed, and costs"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The court may order a party to pay the costs of a summary judgment motion on a substantial indemnity basis if “the party acted unreasonably by making or responding to the motion” or “the party acted in bad faith for the purpose of delay.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 20.06)
```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:5.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Simplified procedure: when it applies"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The simplified procedure in Rule 76 “shall be used” in an action when the plaintiff's claim is exclusively for money, real property or personal property, and the total of the money claimed and the fair market value of the property “is $200,000 or less exclusive of interest and costs”. Property value is taken as at the date the action is commenced. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 76.02 (1))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:5.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Simplified procedure: when it applies"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
With two or more plaintiffs, each plaintiff's claim is considered separately. With two or more defendants, the claim against each defendant is considered separately. In any other action, the procedure “may be used” at the option of the plaintiff, subject to subrules (4) to (9). The statement of claim or notice of action “shall indicate” that the action is brought under Rule 76. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 76.02 (2), (2.1), (3), (4))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:5.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Simplified procedure: when it applies"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Rule 76 does not apply to class proceedings, to actions under the Construction Act “except trust claims”, to actions assigned for case management under rule 77.05, or to actions where a jury notice is delivered under subrule 76.02.1 (2). (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 76.01 (1))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:5.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Simplified procedure: when it applies"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
An action started under Rule 76 stops proceeding under it if, among other things, a defendant objects in the statement of defence that the claim does not meet the conditions and the plaintiff does not abandon, in the reply, the parts that do not comply. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 76.02 (5))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:6:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Simplified procedure: how it differs from an ordinary action
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:6.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Simplified procedure: how it differs from an ordinary action"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Within 10 days after the close of pleadings, each party serves an affidavit of documents and copies of the documents in its Schedule A. The affidavit includes a list of people who might reasonably be expected to know about matters in issue. A party may not call an undisclosed person as a witness at trial “unless the court orders otherwise.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 76.03 (1), (2), (3))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:6.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Simplified procedure: how it differs from an ordinary action"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Written discovery, cross-examination on an affidavit, and examination of a witness on a motion are not permitted. No party may “exceed a total of three hours of examination” in oral discovery. An action under Rule 76 “shall not be tried with a jury”. A jury notice may be delivered only for listed claims such as slander and libel, and the action then “may no longer proceed under this Rule”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 76.04 (1), (2), r. 76.02.1 (1)-(3))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:6.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Simplified procedure: how it differs from an ordinary action"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The plaintiff sets the action down for trial within 180 days after the first defence or notice of intent to defend is filed. The trial management plan's total time “shall not exceed five days”. In an action started on or after January 1, 2020, no party may recover costs exceeding $50,000 or disbursements exceeding $25,000, exclusive of HST, except as Rule 76.13 or an Act provides. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 76.09 (1), r. 76.10 (2), r. 76.12.1 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:6.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Simplified procedure: how it differs from an ordinary action"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
Under Rule 76, the registrar “shall make an order granting the relief sought” on certain motions that are on consent, or have no responding material, where the filed material states that no affected party is under disability, including motions for “setting aside the noting of a party in default” and “setting aside a default judgment”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 76.05 (4), (5))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:7:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Family summary judgment: when it is available"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
“After the respondent has served an answer or after the time for serving an answer has expired, a party may make a motion for summary judgment for a final order without a trial on all or part of any claim made or any defence presented in the case.” (Family Law Rules, r. 16 (1))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:7.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Family summary judgment: when it is available"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The motion “may be made in any case (including a child protection case) that does not include a divorce claim.” In a case with a divorce claim, the uncontested divorce procedure in rule 36 may be used, or the divorce claim may be split from the rest of the case. (Family Law Rules, r. 16 (2), (3))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:8:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide

```
Family summary judgment: evidence and how the court decides
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:8.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Family summary judgment: evidence and how the court decides"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
The party making the motion serves “an affidavit or other evidence that sets out specific facts showing that there is no genuine issue requiring a trial.” The responding party “may not rest on mere allegations or denials” but sets out specific facts showing a genuine issue for trial. (Family Law Rules, r. 16 (4), (4.1))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:8.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Family summary judgment: evidence and how the court decides"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
“If there is no genuine issue requiring a trial of a claim or defence, the court shall make a final order accordingly.” The court may weigh the evidence, evaluate credibility and draw reasonable inferences, and may order oral evidence. If a party's evidence is not from a person with personal knowledge, “the court may draw conclusions unfavourable to the party.” (Family Law Rules, r. 16 (5), (6), (6.1), (6.2))
```

### `guide:summary-judgment-and-simplified-procedure:8.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Summary judgment and simplified procedure, "Family summary judgment: evidence and how the court decides"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/900194

```
“If the only genuine issue is the amount to which a party is entitled, the court shall order a trial to decide the amount.” If the only genuine issue is a question of law, the court decides it. If no final order is made, the court may specify facts not in dispute, state the issues and give directions. (Family Law Rules, r. 16 (7), (8), (9))
```

```
Separately, the court may, on motion, “decide a question of law before trial, if the decision may dispose of all or part of the case, substantially shorten the trial or save substantial costs”. It may also strike out an application, answer or reply “because it sets out no reasonable claim or defence in law”, or dismiss or suspend a case for reasons listed in the rule. (Family Law Rules, r. 16 (12))
```

```
On that kind of motion, “evidence is admissible only if the parties consent or the court gives permission.” (Family Law Rules, r. 16 (13))
```

### `guide:evidence:title`

```
Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits
```

### `guide:evidence:intro`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
This guide sets out what Ontario's Evidence Act and the court rules say about witnesses, documents, records and affidavits in Small Claims Court, in civil cases in the Superior Court of Justice, and in family cases. Each statement is taken from the Act or rule cited after it.
```

### `guide:evidence:1:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
Who can be a witness, and oaths and affirmations
```

### `guide:evidence:1.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Who can be a witness, and oaths and affirmations"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
The Evidence Act is an Ontario statute about evidence. It says “This Act applies to all actions and other matters whatsoever respecting which the Legislature has jurisdiction.” In the Act, “court” “includes a judge, arbitrator, umpire, commissioner, justice of the peace or other officer or person having by law or by consent of parties authority to hear, receive and examine evidence”. (Evidence Act, ss. 1, 2)
```

### `guide:evidence:1.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Who can be a witness, and oaths and affirmations"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
The Act says “A person of any age is presumed to be competent to give evidence.” It also says every person offered as a witness “shall be admitted to give evidence although he or she has an interest in the matter in question or in the event of the action and although he or she has been previously convicted of a crime or offence.” (Evidence Act, ss. 7, 18 (1))
```

### `guide:evidence:1.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Who can be a witness, and oaths and affirmations"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
The parties to an action are, except as the Act otherwise provides, “competent and compellable to give evidence on behalf of themselves or of any of the parties”. The Act says the same of the parties' spouses, who are “competent and compellable to give evidence on behalf of any of the parties.” For this Act, “spouse” means a spouse as defined in section 1 of the Family Law Act. (Evidence Act, ss. 1, 8 (1))
```

### `guide:evidence:1.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Who can be a witness, and oaths and affirmations"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
One limit concerns what a spouse said: “A person is not compellable to disclose any communication made to the person by his or her spouse during the marriage.” (Evidence Act, s. 11)
```

### `guide:evidence:1.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Who can be a witness, and oaths and affirmations"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
“Every court has power to administer or cause to be administered an oath or affirmation to every witness who is called to give evidence before the court.” The Act also says “A person may, instead of taking an oath, make an affirmation or declaration that is of the same force and effect as if the person had taken an oath in the usual form.” (Evidence Act, ss. 3 (2), 17 (1))
```

### `guide:evidence:1.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Who can be a witness, and oaths and affirmations"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
“A witness shall not be excused from answering any question upon the ground that the answer may tend to criminate the witness”, or may tend to establish liability to a civil proceeding or to a prosecution under an Act of the Legislature. (Evidence Act, s. 9 (1))
```

### `guide:evidence:1.7`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Who can be a witness, and oaths and affirmations"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
If the witness objects on those grounds, would have been excused but for this section or a federal Act, and is made to answer, “the answer so given shall not be used or receivable in evidence against him or her in any civil proceeding or in any proceeding under any Act of the Legislature.” (Evidence Act, s. 9 (2))
```

### `guide:evidence:2:heading`

```
Business records, electronic records and copies of documents
```

### `guide:evidence:2.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Business records, electronic records and copies of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
Section 35 of the Evidence Act deals with business records. There, “business” includes “every kind of business, profession, occupation, calling, operation or activity, whether carried on for profit or otherwise”. A “record” “includes any information that is recorded or stored by means of any device.” (Evidence Act, s. 35 (1))
```

### `guide:evidence:2.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Business records, electronic records and copies of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
Under section 35, “Any writing or record made of any act, transaction, occurrence or event is admissible as evidence of such act, transaction, occurrence or event if made in the usual and ordinary course of any business”, and if it was in the usual and ordinary course of that business to make it at the time, “or within a reasonable time thereafter.” (Evidence Act, s. 35 (2))
```

### `guide:evidence:2.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Business records, electronic records and copies of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
This rule applies only if “the party tendering the writing or record has given at least seven days notice of the party’s intention to all other parties in the action”. Any party can get the record produced for inspection “within five days after giving notice to produce the same.” The circumstances of making the record, “including lack of personal knowledge by the maker, may be shown to affect its weight, but such circumstances do not affect its admissibility.” (Evidence Act, s. 35 (3), (4))
```

### `guide:evidence:2.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Business records, electronic records and copies of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
An “electronic record” is data recorded or stored in or by a computer system or similar device, and it “includes a display, printout or other output of that data”. “The person seeking to introduce an electronic record has the burden of proving its authenticity by evidence capable of supporting a finding that the electronic record is what the person claims it to be.” (Evidence Act, s. 34.1 (1), (4))
```

### `guide:evidence:2.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Business records, electronic records and copies of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
Where the best evidence rule applies to an electronic record, “it is satisfied on proof of the integrity of the electronic record.” That integrity may be proved by evidence of the integrity of the electronic records system that recorded or stored the data, “or by evidence that reliable encryption techniques were used to support the integrity of the electronic record.” (Evidence Act, s. 34.1 (5), (5.1))
```

### `guide:evidence:2.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Business records, electronic records and copies of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
The Act sets out when the integrity of an electronic records system is proved “In the absence of evidence to the contrary”, and says those matters “may be established by an affidavit given to the best of the deponent’s knowledge and belief.” An adverse party may cross-examine the person who made that affidavit “as of right”. (Evidence Act, s. 34.1 (7), (9), (10))
```

### `guide:evidence:2.7`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Business records, electronic records and copies of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
Section 34 is about photographic copies of items such as a cheque, receipt, agreement, document or record kept or held by a person. It covers an item photographed “in the course of an established practice” of that person of photographing similar items “in order to keep a permanent record thereof”, and then destroyed by or in the presence of that person or their employees, delivered to another person in the ordinary course of business, or lost. (Evidence Act, s. 34 (2))
```

### `guide:evidence:2.8`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Business records, electronic records and copies of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
For such an item, “a print from the photographic film is admissible in evidence in all cases and for all purposes for which the object photographed would have been admissible.” (Evidence Act, s. 34 (2))
```

### `guide:evidence:2.9`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Business records, electronic records and copies of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
Section 55 covers “a telegram, letter, shipping bill, bill of lading, delivery order, receipt, account or other written instrument used in business or other transactions”. A party may give the opposite party notice, “ten days at least before the trial”, that it intends to use a copy as proof of the contents, naming a time and place to inspect it. (Evidence Act, s. 55 (1))
```

### `guide:evidence:2.10`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Business records, electronic records and copies of documents"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
The copy is then enough evidence of the original's contents unless the party who got the notice, “within four days after the time mentioned for such inspection gives notice that the party intends to dispute the correctness or genuineness of the copy at the trial or proceeding, and to require proof of the original”. (Evidence Act, s. 55 (2))
```

### `guide:evidence:3.1`

- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Health reports, expert witnesses, earlier statements and affidavits"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
A “practitioner” includes “a member of a College as defined in subsection 1 (1) of the Regulated Health Professions Act, 1991”. A report signed by a practitioner and obtained by or prepared for a party is admissible “with leave of the court and after at least ten days notice has been given to all other parties”. “Leave” means the court's permission. Unless the court orders otherwise, a party is entitled to a copy of the report when notice is given. (Evidence Act, s. 52 (1)-(3))
```

### `guide:evidence:3.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Health reports, expert witnesses, earlier statements and affidavits"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
“Except by leave of the judge presiding at the trial, a practitioner who signs a report with respect to a party shall not give evidence at the trial unless the report is given to all other parties” as the Act requires. If the court finds the practitioner's evidence “could have been produced as effectively by way of a report”, it may order the party who required the practitioner to attend to pay costs. (Evidence Act, s. 52 (4), (5))
```

### `guide:evidence:3.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Health reports, expert witnesses, earlier statements and affidavits"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
For witnesses who give opinion evidence, the Act says “not more than three of such witnesses may be called upon either side without the leave of the judge or other person presiding.” (Evidence Act, s. 12)
```

### `guide:evidence:3.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Health reports, expert witnesses, earlier statements and affidavits"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
“A witness may be cross-examined as to previous statements made by him or her in writing, or reduced into writing, relative to the matter in question, without the writing being shown to the witness”. If the writing is to be used to contradict the witness, the witness's attention must first be called to the parts to be used. (Evidence Act, s. 20)
```

### `guide:evidence:3.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Health reports, expert witnesses, earlier statements and affidavits"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
If a witness, on cross-examination about an earlier statement that differs from their testimony, does not clearly admit making it, proof may be given that they made it. First, “the circumstances of the supposed statement sufficient to designate the particular occasion shall be mentioned to the witness, and the witness shall be asked whether or not he or she did make such statement.” (Evidence Act, s. 21)
```

### `guide:evidence:3.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Health reports, expert witnesses, earlier statements and affidavits"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
No informality in the heading or other formal parts of an affidavit made before a person authorized to take affidavits “is any objection to its reception in evidence if the court or judge before whom it is tendered thinks proper to receive it.” When evidence is in an affidavit and the person affirms, the person taking it “shall certify that the deponent satisfied him or her that the deponent was a person entitled to affirm.” (Evidence Act, ss. 17 (2), 46)
```

### `guide:evidence:4.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Small Claims Court: what evidence the court may receive"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
The Courts of Justice Act says the Small Claims Court “may admit as evidence at a hearing and act upon any oral testimony and any document or other thing so long as the evidence is relevant to the” subject-matter of the proceeding, “but the court may exclude anything unduly repetitious.” This “applies whether or not the evidence is given or proven under oath or affirmation or admissible as evidence in any other court.” (Courts of Justice Act, s. 27 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:evidence:4.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Small Claims Court: what evidence the court may receive"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
There are limits. Nothing is admissible “that would be inadmissible by reason of any privilege under the law of evidence” or “that is inadmissible by any Act.” The court's power also does not override any Act “expressly limiting the extent to or purposes for which any oral testimony, documents or things may be admitted or used in evidence in any proceeding.” (Courts of Justice Act, s. 27 (3), (4))
```

### `guide:evidence:4.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Small Claims Court: what evidence the court may receive"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
On copies, “A copy of a document or any other thing may be admitted as evidence at a hearing if the presiding judge is satisfied as to its authenticity.” (Courts of Justice Act, s. 27 (5))
```

### `guide:evidence:4.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Small Claims Court: what evidence the court may receive"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
Under the Small Claims Court rules, “At the trial of an undefended action, the plaintiff's case may be proved by affidavit, unless the trial judge orders otherwise.” (Rules of the Small Claims Court, r. 18.01)
```

### `guide:evidence:4.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Small Claims Court: what evidence the court may receive"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
“A document or written statement or an audio or visual record that has been served, at least 30 days before the trial date, on all parties who were served with the notice of trial, shall be received in evidence, unless the trial judge orders otherwise.” (Rules of the Small Claims Court, r. 18.02 (1))
```

### `guide:evidence:4.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Small Claims Court: what evidence the court may receive"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
This covers “The signed written statement of any witness, including the written report of an expert”, to the extent it relates to things the witness could testify to in person. It also covers any other document, “including but not limited to a hospital record or medical report made in the course of care and treatment, a financial record, a receipt, a bill, documentary evidence of loss of income or property damage, and a repair estimate.” (Rules of the Small Claims Court, r. 18.02 (2))
```

- **Status:** draft

- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Small Claims Court: what evidence the court may receive"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
A party serving such a statement or document must include “the name, telephone number and address for service of the witness or author”, and, for an expert, “a summary of his or her qualifications.” A party who was served and wishes to cross-examine the witness or author “may summon him or her as a witness under subrule 18.03 (1).” (Rules of the Small Claims Court, r. 18.02 (3), (4))
```

### `guide:evidence:5.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Small Claims Court: summoning a witness"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
“A party who requires the attendance of a person in Ontario as a witness at a trial may serve the person with a summons to witness (Form 18A)”. The summons may also require the witness to bring to the trial documents or other things in their possession, control or power “relating to the matters in question in the action that are specified in the summons.” (Rules of the Small Claims Court, r. 18.03 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:evidence:5.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Small Claims Court: summoning a witness"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
A summons to witness “shall be served personally by the party who requires the presence of the witness, or by the party's representative, at least 10 days before the trial date”. At the time of service, attendance money calculated under the regulations under the Administration of Justice Act “shall be paid or tendered to the witness.” (Rules of the Small Claims Court, r. 8.01 (7), 18.03 (3))
```

### `guide:evidence:5.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Small Claims Court: summoning a witness"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
A party who serves a summons on a witness or author of a served statement or document must, at the same time, “serve a copy of the summons on every other party.” A party not served with that copy “may request an adjournment of the trial, with costs.” (Rules of the Small Claims Court, r. 18.02 (5), (7))
```

### `guide:evidence:5.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Small Claims Court: summoning a witness"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
If a party summons a witness who needs an interpreter, “the party shall arrange for a qualified interpreter to attend at the trial”, unless the interpretation is between English and French and the Ministry of the Attorney General provides the interpreter. (Rules of the Small Claims Court, r. 18.03 (5.1))
```

### `guide:evidence:5.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** small-claims / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Small Claims Court: summoning a witness"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
If a witness “whose evidence is material to the conduct of an action” does not attend or remain as the summons requires, the trial judge may issue a warrant (Form 18B) to have the witness brought before the court. If a party has “abused the power to summon a witness”, the court may order that party to pay the witness compensation. (Rules of the Small Claims Court, r. 18.03 (6), (8))
```

### `guide:evidence:6.1`

- **Status:** draft

- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Civil cases: witnesses and evidence at trial"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
“Unless these rules provide otherwise, witnesses at the trial of an action shall be examined orally in court and the examination may consist of direct examination, cross-examination and re-examination.” The trial judge “may disallow a question put to a witness that is vexatious or irrelevant”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 53.01 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:evidence:6.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Civil cases: witnesses and evidence at trial"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
Where a witness does not understand the language of the examination, or is deaf or mute, a competent and independent interpreter must take an oath or affirmation before the witness is called. The party calling the witness “shall provide the interpreter”, unless the interpretation is between English and French and the Ministry of the Attorney General provides one. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 53.01 (5), (6))
```

### `guide:evidence:6.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Civil cases: witnesses and evidence at trial"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
The court may allow “the evidence of a witness or proof of a particular fact or document to be given by affidavit, unless an adverse party reasonably requires the attendance of the deponent at trial for cross-examination.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 53.02 (1))
```

### `guide:evidence:6.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Civil cases: witnesses and evidence at trial"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
A party who intends to call an expert witness at trial must, “not less than 90 days before the pre-trial conference”, serve on every other party a report signed by the expert with the listed information. A responding expert's report is due “not less than 60 days before the pre-trial conference”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 53.03 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:evidence:6.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Civil cases: witnesses and evidence at trial"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
Without leave of the trial judge, an expert may not testify on an issue unless the substance of that testimony is set out in a served report, a supplementary report served “not less than 45 days before the commencement of the trial”, or a responding supplementary report served “not less than 15 days before” it. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 53.03 (3))
```

### `guide:evidence:6.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Civil cases: witnesses and evidence at trial"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
These times for serving reports may be extended or abridged by a judge or associate judge at a pre-trial or Rule 77 conference, by the court on motion, or on the parties' written consent, except that the parties may not consent to an extension that would affect the scheduled trial date. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 53.03 (4))
```

### `guide:evidence:6.7`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Civil cases: witnesses and evidence at trial"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
A party may serve a person in Ontario with a summons to witness (Form 53A). It “shall be served on the witness personally”, and at the same time “attendance money calculated in accordance with Tariff A shall be paid or tendered to the witness.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 53.04 (1), (4))
```

### `guide:evidence:6.8`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Civil cases: witnesses and evidence at trial"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
If a witness whose evidence is material was served and paid or tendered proper attendance money, but does not attend or remain as the summons requires, the presiding judge may issue a warrant for arrest (Form 53B) to have the witness apprehended and brought before the court. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 53.04 (7))
```

### `guide:evidence:6.9`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Evidence: witnesses, documents and affidavits, "Civil cases: witnesses and evidence at trial"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90e23

```
A party may call an adverse party as a witness unless that person has already testified or the adverse party or its lawyer undertakes to call them. Attendance is secured by serving a summons, or by serving on the adverse party or their lawyer, “at least 10 days before the commencement of the trial, a notice of intention to call the person as a witness”, and paying or tendering attendance money. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 53.07 (1), (2), (4))
```

- **Status:** draft
