```
Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact
```

### `guide:parenting:intro`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
This guide explains, in general terms, what Ontario’s Children’s Law Reform Act and the federal Divorce Act say about decision-making responsibility, parenting time, contact and the best interests of the child. It describes what the law says; it does not say how a court would decide any particular family’s situation.
```

### `guide:parenting:1:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
Words the law uses
```

### `guide:parenting:1.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Words the law uses"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
In Ontario’s Children’s Law Reform Act, “decision-making responsibility” means “responsibility for making significant decisions about a child’s well-being, including with respect to,” health, education, culture, language, religion and spirituality, and significant extra-curricular activities. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 18 (1))
```

### `guide:parenting:1.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Words the law uses"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
“Parenting time” means “the time a child spends in the care of a parent of the child, whether or not the child is physically with the parent during that time”. “Contact” means “the time a child spends in the care of a person other than the child’s parent, whether or not the child is physically with the person during that time”. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 18 (1))
```

### `guide:parenting:1.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Words the law uses"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The Act says that, unless the context requires otherwise, “a reference in an Act or regulation to custody of a child, including lawful custody or legal custody of a child, includes reference to decision-making responsibility with respect to the child under this Act”. A reference to access to a child includes parenting time or contact. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 18 (5), (6))
```

### `guide:parenting:1.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Words the law uses"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The federal Divorce Act uses the same ideas. It defines decision-making responsibility as “the responsibility for making significant decisions about a child’s well-being”, including health, education, culture, language, religion and spirituality, and significant extra-curricular activities. Parenting time is “the time that a child of the marriage spends in the care of a person referred to in subsection 16.1(1), whether or not the child is physically with that person during that entire time”. (Divorce Act, s. 2 (1))
```

### `guide:parenting:2:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
Which Act, and who can apply
```

### `guide:parenting:2.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Which Act, and who can apply"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The Divorce Act deals with a “child of the marriage”. That means “a child of two spouses or former spouses who, at the material time,” is under the age of majority and has not withdrawn from their charge, or is the age of majority or over and under their charge but unable, by reason of illness, disability or other cause, to withdraw from their charge or to obtain the necessaries of life. (Divorce Act, s. 2 (1))
```

### `guide:parenting:2.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Which Act, and who can apply"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
For Ontario, “court” in the Divorce Act means “the Superior Court of Justice”. The definition also includes any other court in the province whose judges are appointed by the Governor General and that the province designates as a court for the purposes of the Act. (Divorce Act, s. 2 (1))
```

### `guide:parenting:2.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Which Act, and who can apply"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
Under the Divorce Act, a court may make a parenting order on application by “either or both spouses” or by “a person, other than a spouse, who is a parent of the child, stands in the place of a parent or intends to stand in the place of a parent.” A person in that second group may apply “only with leave of the court.” (Divorce Act, s. 16.1 (1), (3))
```

### `guide:parenting:2.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Which Act, and who can apply"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
Under the Children’s Law Reform Act, “A parent of a child may apply to a court for a parenting order respecting,” decision-making responsibility and parenting time. Any person other than a parent, “including a grandparent,” may apply for a parenting order about decision-making responsibility, or for a contact order. In this Part of the Act, “court” means “the Ontario Court of Justice, the Family Court or the Superior Court of Justice”. (Children’s Law Reform Act, ss. 18 (1), 21 (1)-(3))
```

### `guide:parenting:2.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Which Act, and who can apply"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
If a divorce action is started under the Divorce Act, an application under this Part of the Children’s Law Reform Act about decision-making responsibility, parenting time or contact that has not been determined “is stayed except by leave of the court.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 27)
```

### `guide:parenting:2.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Which Act, and who can apply"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
A person applying under the Children’s Law Reform Act for a parenting order or contact order files an affidavit with “the person’s proposed plan for the child’s care and upbringing”, information about their involvement in any family proceedings or criminal proceedings, and other information relevant to the best-interests factors in section 24. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 21 (4))
```

### `guide:parenting:2.7`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Which Act, and who can apply"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
Neither Act, in the text this site holds, contains one general statement that sorts parents into one Act or the other by whether they were married. This site does not yet have a source for such a rule. (Children’s Law Reform Act, ss. 21, 27; Divorce Act, ss. 2 (1), 16.1)
```

### `guide:parenting:3:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The best interests of the child
```

### `guide:parenting:3.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "The best interests of the child"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
In making a parenting order or contact order, the court “shall only take into account the best interests of the child in accordance with this section.” The court considers all factors related to the child’s circumstances and gives “primary consideration to the child’s physical, emotional and psychological safety, security and well-being.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 24 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:parenting:3.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "The best interests of the child"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The listed factors include the child’s needs, given age and stage of development, “such as the child’s need for stability”; the nature and strength of the child’s relationship with each parent, siblings, grandparents and other important people; “each parent’s willingness to support the development and maintenance of the child’s relationship with the other parent”; the history of care of the child; and “the child’s views and preferences, giving due weight to the child’s age and maturity, unless they cannot be ascertained”. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 24 (3))
```

### `guide:parenting:3.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "The best interests of the child"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
Other listed factors are the child’s cultural, linguistic, religious and spiritual upbringing and heritage, “including Indigenous upbringing and heritage”; any plans for the child’s care; the ability and willingness of each person the order would apply to, to care for and meet the child’s needs and to communicate and co-operate; any family violence and its impact; and “any civil or criminal proceeding, order, condition or measure that is relevant to the safety, security and well-being of the child.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 24 (3))
```

### `guide:parenting:3.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "The best interests of the child"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The court “shall not take into consideration the past conduct of any person, unless the conduct is relevant to the exercise of the person’s decision-making responsibility, parenting time or contact with respect to the child.” In allocating parenting time, the court applies the principle that “a child should have as much time with each parent as is consistent with the best interests of the child.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 24 (5), (6))
```

### `guide:parenting:3.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "The best interests of the child"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The Divorce Act has the same structure. “The court shall take into consideration only the best interests of the child of the marriage in making a parenting order or a contact order.” It lists factors in nearly the same words, speaking of each “spouse” where the Ontario Act speaks of each “parent”, and it applies the principle that “a child should have as much time with each spouse as is consistent with the best interests of the child.” (Divorce Act, s. 16 (1), (3), (6))
```

### `guide:parenting:4:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
Family violence
```

### `guide:parenting:4.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Family violence"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The Children’s Law Reform Act defines family violence as “any conduct by a family member towards another family member that is violent or threatening, that constitutes a pattern of coercive and controlling behaviour, or that causes the other family member to fear for their own safety or for that of another person, and, in the case of a child, includes direct or indirect exposure to such conduct”. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 18 (1))
```

### `guide:parenting:4.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Family violence"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The conduct “need not constitute a criminal offence”. It includes physical abuse (including forced confinement, but not reasonable force to protect oneself or another person), sexual abuse, threats to kill or cause bodily harm, harassment including stalking, failure to provide the necessaries of life, psychological abuse, financial abuse, threats to kill or harm an animal or damage property, and killing or harming an animal or damaging property. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 18 (2))
```

### `guide:parenting:4.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Family violence"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
When considering the impact of family violence, the court takes into account, among other things, “the nature, seriousness and frequency of the family violence and when it occurred”; “whether there is a pattern of coercive and controlling behaviour in relation to a family member”; whether the child is exposed to it; “the physical, emotional and psychological harm or risk of harm to the child”; safety and fear; steps taken to prevent further violence; and “any other relevant factor.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 24 (4))
```

### `guide:parenting:4.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Family violence"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The court also takes into account any compromise to the safety of the child or other family member; whether the violence causes the child or other family member to fear for their own safety or that of another person; any steps taken by the person engaging in the violence “to prevent further family violence from occurring and improve the person’s ability to care for and meet the needs of the child”; and “any other relevant factor.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 24 (4))
```

### `guide:parenting:4.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Family violence"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The Divorce Act defines family violence in similar words, covering conduct “whether or not the conduct constitutes a criminal offence”, and lists the same kinds of conduct. It sets out the same factors for the court to consider about the impact of family violence. (Divorce Act, ss. 2 (1), 16 (4))
```

### `guide:parenting:5:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
What a parenting or contact order can say
```

### `guide:parenting:5.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "What a parenting or contact order can say"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
On an application under section 21, the court may grant decision-making responsibility to one or more persons, parenting time to one or more parents of the child, or contact to one or more persons other than a parent, according to the kind of application made under that section. It may “determine any aspect of the incidents of the right to decision-making responsibility, parenting time or contact”. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 28 (1) (a), (b))
```

### `guide:parenting:5.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "What a parenting or contact order can say"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The court may also make “any additional order the court considers necessary and proper in the circumstances”. The listed examples include orders limiting the duration, frequency, manner or location of contact or communication between any of the parties, or between a party and the child, and prohibiting a party or other person from engaging in specified conduct in the child’s presence or at any time when the person is responsible for the child’s care. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 28 (1) (c))
```

### `guide:parenting:5.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "What a parenting or contact order can say"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
Other listed examples are orders prohibiting a party from changing the child’s residence, school or day care facility, or removing the child from Ontario, without another party’s consent or a court order; requiring delivery of the child’s passport, health card or another specified document; requiring a party to give, or consent to the release of, information about the child’s well-being; and requiring a party to facilitate the child’s communication with another party or person. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 28 (1) (c))
```

### `guide:parenting:5.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "What a parenting or contact order can say"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The court may allocate decision-making responsibility, “or any aspect of it, to one or more persons”, and may allocate parenting time “by way of a schedule.” Unless the court orders otherwise, a person with parenting time “has exclusive authority during that time to make day-to-day decisions affecting the child.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 28 (4)-(6))
```

### `guide:parenting:5.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "What a parenting or contact order can say"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The court includes in a parenting order or contact order any written parenting plan the parties submit with the elements they agree on, “subject to any changes the court may specify if it considers it to be in the best interests of the child to do so.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 28 (7))
```

### `guide:parenting:5.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "What a parenting or contact order can say"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
Unless a court orders otherwise, a person granted decision-making responsibility or parenting time under a parenting order may ask for and, “subject to any applicable laws”, receive information about the child’s well-being, including health and education. The information may come from any other person granted decision-making responsibility or parenting time under a parenting order, or from any other person likely to have it. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 28 (8))
```

### `guide:parenting:5.7`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "What a parenting or contact order can say"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The Divorce Act gives similar powers. An order may allocate parenting time and decision-making responsibility, may “require that parenting time or the transfer of the child from one person to another be supervised”, and may “authorize or prohibit the relocation of the child.” A contact order can be made on application by “a person other than a spouse”, with leave of the court unless leave was already obtained under section 16.1. (Divorce Act, ss. 16.1 (4), (7), (8), 16.5 (1), (3))
```

### `guide:parenting:5.8`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "What a parenting or contact order can say"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
In deciding on a contact order under the Divorce Act, the court considers all relevant factors, “including whether contact between the applicant and the child could otherwise occur, for example during the parenting time of another person.” (Divorce Act, s. 16.5 (4))
```

### `guide:parenting:5.9`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "What a parenting or contact order can say"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The Divorce Act also sets out duties. A person with parenting time, decision-making responsibility or contact “shall exercise that time, responsibility or contact in a manner that is consistent with the best interests of the child.” A party “shall, to the best of their ability, protect any child of the marriage from conflict arising from the proceeding.” (Divorce Act, ss. 7.1, 7.2)
```

### `guide:parenting:6:heading`

- **Status:** draft

- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
Changing an existing order
```

### `guide:parenting:6.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Changing an existing order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
Under the Children’s Law Reform Act, a court shall not vary a parenting order or contact order “unless there has been a material change in circumstances that affects or is likely to affect the best interests of the child who is the subject of the order.” A relocation in accordance with section 39.4 is a material change in circumstances. If a court had prohibited the relocation, it “does not, in itself, constitute a material change in circumstances.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 29 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:parenting:6.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Changing an existing order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
Under the Divorce Act, before varying a parenting order or contact order, the court shall “satisfy itself that there has been a change in the circumstances of the child since the making of the order or the last variation order made in respect of the order”. The relocation of a child is deemed to be a change in circumstances, but a relocation a court has prohibited is not, in itself, such a change. (Divorce Act, s. 17 (5), (5.2), (5.3))
```

```
Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act
```

### `guide:parenting:7.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The Act defines “relocation” as a change in residence of the child, or of a person with decision-making responsibility or parenting time (or an applicant for a parenting order), that “is likely to have a significant impact on the child’s relationship with” another such person or a person who has contact under a contact order. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 18 (1))
```

### `guide:parenting:7.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
For a change in residence that is not a relocation, a person with decision-making responsibility or parenting time must notify any other person who has decision-making responsibility, parenting time or contact under a contact order. The notice must be in writing and set out the expected date of the change and the new address and contact information. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 39.1 (1), (2), (5))
```

### `guide:parenting:7.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
For a relocation, a person with decision-making responsibility or parenting time must give the notice “at least 60 days before the expected date of the proposed relocation”. It is in the form prescribed by the regulations or, if no form is prescribed, in writing. It sets out the expected date, the new address and contact information, “a proposal as to how decision-making responsibility, parenting time or contact, as the case may be, could be exercised”, and any other information the regulations prescribe. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 39.3 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:parenting:7.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
On application, the court may provide that the notice rules do not apply, or apply with changes it specifies, if it is of the opinion that it is appropriate to do so, “including if there is a risk of family violence.” That application “may be made without notice to any other party.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, ss. 39.1 (3), (4), 39.2 (4), (5), 39.3 (3), (4))
```

### `guide:parenting:7.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
A person with decision-making responsibility or parenting time who receives a relocation notice may, “no later than 30 days after receiving the notice,” object by notifying the person who gave it, in writing with reasons and their views on the proposal, or by making an application under section 21. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 39.3 (5), (6))
```

### `guide:parenting:7.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
A person who has given notice of a proposed relocation in accordance with section 39.3 may relocate the child as of the date in the notice if the relocation is authorized by a court, or if no objection is made in accordance with subsection 39.3 (5) “and there is no order prohibiting the relocation.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 39.4 (2))
```

### `guide:parenting:7.7`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
In deciding whether to authorize a relocation, the court considers the best interests of the child under section 24, and also factors that include the reasons for the relocation, its impact on the child, and the time spent with the child, and involvement in the child’s life, of each person with parenting time or a pending parenting application. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 39.4 (3))
```

### `guide:parenting:7.8`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The court also considers whether the person who intends to relocate the child complied with the notice requirements and any applicable Act, regulation, order, award or agreement; any order, award or agreement specifying where the child is to reside; the reasonableness of the proposal, including travel expenses; and each person’s compliance with their obligations and likelihood of future compliance. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 39.4 (3) (d)-(g))
```

### `guide:parenting:7.9`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The court “shall not consider whether, if the child’s relocation were to be prohibited, the person who intends to relocate the child would relocate without the child or not relocate.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 39.4 (4))
```

### `guide:parenting:7.10`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
If the parties substantially comply with an order, family arbitration award or agreement providing that the child spend “substantially equal time in the care of each party”, the party who intends to relocate the child must prove the relocation would be in the child’s best interests. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 39.4 (5))
```

### `guide:parenting:7.11`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
If they substantially comply with one providing that the child spend “the vast majority of time” in the care of the party who intends to relocate, the opposing party must prove the relocation would not be in the child’s best interests. In any other case, both parties have the burden of proving whether it is. (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 39.4 (6), (7))
```

### `guide:parenting:7.12`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
If the order behind either of the first two burden rules is an interim order, “the court may determine that the subsection does not apply.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 39.4 (8))
```

### `guide:parenting:7.13`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Children’s Law Reform Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
A person who has contact under a contact order and intends to change residence must also give written notice to each person with decision-making responsibility or parenting time. If the change is likely to have a significant impact on the child’s relationship with that person, the notice is given “at least 60 days before the date on which the change is expected to occur.” (Children’s Law Reform Act, s. 39.2 (1)-(3))
```

- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The Divorce Act has parallel rules. For a change of residence that is not a relocation, written notice sets out the expected date and the new address and contact information. For a relocation, notice is given “at least 60 days before the expected date of the proposed relocation and in the form prescribed by the regulations”. (Divorce Act, ss. 16.7, 16.8 (1), (2), 16.9 (1), (2))
```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Divorce Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
The court may, on application, provide that the notice requirements do not apply or modify them, “including where there is a risk of family violence.” The application may be made without notice to any other party. (Divorce Act, ss. 16.8 (3), (4), 16.9 (3), (4))
```

### `guide:parenting:8.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Divorce Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c12

```
A person with parenting time or decision-making responsibility who has received a relocation notice may object “within 30 days after the day on which the notice is received”, in a prescribed form or in an application under subsection 16.1(1) or paragraph 17(1)(b). The person who gave notice under section 16.9 may relocate the child as of the date in the notice if a court authorizes it, or if there is no such objection and no order prohibiting the relocation. (Divorce Act, s. 16.91 (1))
```

- **Appears in:** Guides, Parenting: decision-making, parenting time and contact, "Moving: notice rules under the Divorce Act"

```
In deciding whether to authorize a relocation, the court considers, “in addition to the factors referred to in section 16,” a list of factors in close to the same words as the Ontario Act. The burden-of-proof rules are also parallel, and a court “may decide not to apply” the first two of them if the order involved is an interim order. (Divorce Act, ss. 16.92, 16.93, 16.94)
```

### `guide:child-support:intro`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
This guide explains, in general terms, what Ontario’s Family Law Act, the federal Divorce Act and the child support guidelines say about child support and how the amount is worked out. It does not calculate any amount and does not say what any particular person would pay or receive.
```

### `guide:child-support:1:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The duty to support a child under the Family Law Act
```

### `guide:child-support:1.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "The duty to support a child under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Ontario’s Family Law Act says “Every parent has an obligation to provide support, to the extent that the parent is capable of doing so, for his or her unmarried child who,” is a minor, is enrolled in a full-time program of education, or is unable by reason of illness, disability or other cause to withdraw from parental care. The obligation “does not extend to a child who is sixteen years of age or older and has withdrawn from parental control.” (Family Law Act, s. 31 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:child-support:1.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "The duty to support a child under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The obligation does not extend to a child “who is sixteen years of age or older and has withdrawn from parental control.” (Family Law Act, s. 31 (2))
```

### `guide:child-support:1.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "The duty to support a child under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
“A court may, on application, order a person to provide support for his or her dependants and determine the amount of support.” A dependant is “a person to whom another has an obligation to provide support under this Part”. The application may be made by “the dependant or the dependant’s parent”, and in some cases by an agency that provides social assistance or disability support for the dependant. (Family Law Act, ss. 29, 33 (1)-(3))
```

### `guide:child-support:1.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "The duty to support a child under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
An order for the support of a child should “recognize that each parent has an obligation to provide support for the child” and apportion the obligation according to the child support guidelines. A court making the order “shall do so in accordance with the child support guidelines.” (Family Law Act, s. 33 (7), (11))
```

### `guide:child-support:1.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "The duty to support a child under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The Act allows a different amount in two situations. The first is where special provisions in an order or written agreement benefit the child and the guidelines amount would be “inequitable given those special provisions”; the court records its reasons. The second is on the consent of both parents, where “reasonable arrangements have been made for the support of the child” and, if support for the child is payable out of public money, the arrangements do not provide for less than the guidelines amount. (Family Law Act, s. 33 (12)-(14))
```

### `guide:child-support:1.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "The duty to support a child under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
When a divorce proceeding is started under the Divorce Act, a support application under this Part of the Family Law Act that has not been adjudicated “is stayed, unless the court orders otherwise.” (Family Law Act, s. 36 (1))
```

### `guide:child-support:2:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Child support under the Divorce Act
```

### `guide:child-support:2.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Child support under the Divorce Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Under the federal Divorce Act, “A court of competent jurisdiction may, on application by either or both spouses, make an order requiring a spouse to pay for the support of any or all children of the marriage.” The court may also make an interim order while the application is pending. (Divorce Act, s. 15.1 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:child-support:2.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Child support under the Divorce Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The court makes the order “in accordance with the applicable guidelines.” It may award a different amount where special provisions benefit the child and the guidelines amount would be inequitable, or on the consent of both spouses if “reasonable arrangements have been made for the support of the child”. (Divorce Act, s. 15.1 (3), (5), (7))
```

### `guide:child-support:2.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Child support under the Divorce Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Arrangements are not unreasonable “solely because the amount of support agreed to is not the same as the amount that would otherwise have been determined in accordance with the applicable guidelines.” (Divorce Act, s. 15.1 (8))
```

### `guide:child-support:2.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Child support under the Divorce Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Where a court is considering applications for both child support and spousal support, “the court shall give priority to child support in determining the applications.” (Divorce Act, s. 15.3 (1))
```

### `guide:child-support:3.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Which guidelines and which table"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The Divorce Act defines “applicable guidelines”. If both spouses habitually reside in the same province at the time the application is made and that province has been designated by an order under subsection 2 (5), they are “the laws of the province specified in the order”. Otherwise (“in any other case”), they are the Federal Child Support Guidelines. (Divorce Act, s. 2 (1), (5))
```

### `guide:child-support:3.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Which guidelines and which table"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
This site does not yet have a source on disk that says whether Ontario has been designated under that subsection. (Divorce Act, s. 2 (5))
```

### `guide:child-support:3.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Which guidelines and which table"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Ontario’s regulation covers both kinds of case. In it, “child” means a dependant under the Family Law Act or, “in cases where the Divorce Act (Canada) applies, a child of the marriage under that Act”. In a Divorce Act case, “spouse” means “either of two persons who are married to each other and includes a former spouse”. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 2 (1))
```

### `guide:child-support:3.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Which guidelines and which table"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Under the Ontario regulation, the “table” is a table in the Federal Child Support Guidelines. If the parent or spouse against whom the order is sought ordinarily resides in Ontario at the time of the application, it is “the table set out in the Federal Child Support Guidelines for Ontario”; if elsewhere in Canada, the table for that province or territory. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 2 (1), (1.1))
```

### `guide:child-support:3.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Which guidelines and which table"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The Ontario regulation has further rules for a change of residence since the application, a move expected in the near future, and a parent or spouse who resides outside Canada or whose residence is unknown. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 2 (1))
```

### `guide:child-support:3.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Which guidelines and which table"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The Federal Child Support Guidelines also choose the applicable table by where the spouse against whom the order is sought habitually resides, with rules for a change of province, a move expected in the near future, and a spouse who resides outside Canada or whose residence is unknown. (Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 3 (3))
```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The basic amount: the table amount
```

### `guide:child-support:4.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "The basic amount: the table amount"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Unless the guidelines provide otherwise, the amount for children under the age of majority is “the amount set out in the applicable table, according to the number of children under the age of majority to whom the order relates and the income of the parent or spouse against whom the order is sought”, plus any amount under section 7. The federal wording is the same except that it refers only to the spouse. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 3 (1); Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 3 (1))
```

### `guide:child-support:4.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "The basic amount: the table amount"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
For a child who is the age of majority or over, the amount is found by applying the guidelines as if the child were under that age, or, if the court considers that inappropriate, the amount it considers appropriate “having regard to the condition, means, needs and other circumstances of the child and the financial ability of each parent or spouse to contribute to the support of the child.” (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 3 (2))
```

### `guide:child-support:4.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "The basic amount: the table amount"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Where the income of the person against whom the order is sought is over $150,000, the amount is the section 3 amount or, if the court considers that inappropriate, the table amount on the first $150,000 plus an amount the court considers appropriate on the balance, plus any section 7 amount. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 4; Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 4)
```

### `guide:child-support:4.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "The basic amount: the table amount"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Where medical or dental insurance for the child is available to either parent or spouse “through his or her employer or otherwise at a reasonable rate, the court may order that coverage be acquired or continued.” (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 6; Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 6)
```

### `guide:child-support:4.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "The basic amount: the table amount"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
This guide does not calculate any amount. The guidelines say that an order must include, among other things, the income of any parent or spouse whose income is used and the amount determined under the table. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 13; Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 13)
```

### `guide:child-support:5:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Special or extraordinary expenses
```

### `guide:child-support:5.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Special or extraordinary expenses"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
On request, the court may provide for an amount to cover all or part of certain expenses, “taking into account the necessity of the expense in relation to the child’s best interests and the reasonableness of the expense in relation to the means of the parents or spouses and those of the child”, and to the spending pattern during cohabitation. The federal wording refers to “the family’s spending pattern prior to the separation”. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 7 (1); Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 7 (1))
```

### `guide:child-support:5.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Special or extraordinary expenses"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The listed expenses are: child care expenses related to the employment, illness, disability or education or training for employment of the parent or spouse with the majority of parenting time; the child’s portion of medical and dental insurance premiums; health-related expenses “that exceed insurance reimbursement by at least $100 annually”; extraordinary expenses for primary or secondary school or other educational programs meeting the child’s particular needs; post-secondary education expenses; and extraordinary expenses for extracurricular activities. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 7 (1))
```

### `guide:child-support:5.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Special or extraordinary expenses"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
For school and extracurricular expenses, “extraordinary expenses” means expenses that exceed what the requesting parent or spouse can reasonably cover, taking into account their income and the table amount they would receive (or the amount the court has otherwise determined is appropriate). (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 7 (1.1); Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 7 (1.1))
```

### `guide:child-support:5.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Special or extraordinary expenses"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Where that does not apply, the court considers the amount of the expense relative to the requesting person’s income, the nature and number of programs and activities, any special needs and talents of the child, the overall cost, and other similar factors. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 7 (1.1); Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 7 (1.1))
```

### `guide:child-support:5.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Special or extraordinary expenses"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
“The guiding principle” is that the expense “is shared by the parents or spouses in proportion to their respective incomes after deducting from the expense, the contribution, if any, from the child.” The court takes into account subsidies, benefits and income tax deductions or credits relating to the expense, and any eligibility to claim them, but not any universal child care benefit or eligibility to claim it. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 7 (2)-(4))
```

### `guide:child-support:6:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Split and shared parenting time
```

### `guide:child-support:6.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Split and shared parenting time"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
In the guidelines, “majority of parenting time” means “a period of time that is more than 60 per cent of parenting time over the course of a year”. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 2 (1))
```

### `guide:child-support:6.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Split and shared parenting time"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Split parenting time: if there are two or more children and each parent or spouse has the majority of parenting time with one or more of them, the amount is “the difference between the amount that each parent or spouse would otherwise pay if such an order were sought against each of the parents or spouses.” The federal guidelines say the same thing in slightly different words. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 8; Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 8)
```

### `guide:child-support:6.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Split and shared parenting time"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Shared parenting time: where each parent or spouse exercises parenting time “for not less than 40 per cent of the time over the course of a year”, the amount is determined by taking into account the table amounts for each of them, “the increased costs of shared parenting time arrangements”, and the condition, means, needs and other circumstances of each of them and of the child. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 9; Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 9)
```

### `guide:child-support:7:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Undue hardship
```

### `guide:child-support:7.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Undue hardship"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
On the application of either spouse (or, under the Ontario regulation, an applicant under section 33 of the Family Law Act), a court may award a different amount from the amount under sections 3 to 5, 8 or 9 “if the court finds that the parent or spouse making the request, or a child in respect of whom the request is made, would otherwise suffer undue hardship.” (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 10 (1); Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 10 (1))
```

### `guide:child-support:7.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Undue hardship"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Listed circumstances that may cause undue hardship include an “unusually high level of debts reasonably incurred” to support the family during cohabitation or to earn a living; “unusually high expenses in relation to exercising parenting time with respect to a child”; a legal duty under a judgment, order or written separation agreement to support any person; and a legal duty to support other children, or a person unable to obtain the necessaries of life due to illness or disability. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 10 (2))
```

### `guide:child-support:7.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Undue hardship"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Even if undue hardship is found, the application “must be denied” if the court is of the opinion that the household of the person claiming undue hardship would, after child support is determined under sections 3 to 5, 8 or 9, have a higher standard of living than the other household. The court may use the test in Schedule II to compare. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 10 (3), (4); Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 10 (3), (4))
```

### `guide:child-support:7.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Undue hardship"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Where the court orders a different amount because of undue hardship, it “must record its reasons for doing so.” (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 10 (6); Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 10 (6))
```

### `guide:child-support:8:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
How income is determined
```

### `guide:child-support:8.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "How income is determined"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Income is determined using the sources of income under the heading “Total income” in the T1 General form issued by the Canada Revenue Agency, adjusted under Schedule III, subject to sections 17 to 20. If both agree in writing on a person’s income, the court may use that amount if it is reasonable given the income information provided. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, ss. 15, 16; Federal Child Support Guidelines, ss. 15, 16)
```

### `guide:child-support:8.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "How income is determined"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
If the section 16 figure “would not be the fairest determination of that income”, the court may look at income over the last three years. Special rules apply to a shareholder, director or officer of a corporation. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, ss. 17 (1), 18 (1))
```

### `guide:child-support:8.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "How income is determined"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
“The court may impute such amount of income to a parent or spouse as it considers appropriate in the circumstances”. Listed circumstances include being intentionally under-employed or unemployed (with exceptions for a child’s needs or the person’s reasonable educational or health needs), income diverted, and having “failed to provide income information when under a legal obligation to do so”. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 19 (1))
```

### `guide:child-support:8.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "How income is determined"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
An applicant whose income information is necessary to determine the amount includes with the application income tax returns and notices of assessment and reassessment “for each of the three most recent taxation years”, and other listed documents. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 21 (1); Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 21 (1))
```

### `guide:child-support:8.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "How income is determined"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
A person served with the application whose income information is necessary must provide those documents to the court and the other party “within 30 days after the application is served” if they reside in Canada or the United States, or within 60 days if they reside elsewhere, or another time the court specifies. (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 21 (2); Federal Child Support Guidelines, s. 21 (2))
```

### `guide:child-support:9:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Changing a child support order
```

### `guide:child-support:9.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Changing a child support order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Where the amount includes a table determination, a change of circumstances for a variation includes “any change in circumstances that would result in a different order for the support of a child or any provision thereof.” Where it does not, it includes “any change in the condition, means, needs or other circumstances of either parent or spouse or of any child who is entitled to support.” (Child Support Guidelines, O. Reg. 391/97, s. 14)
```

### `guide:child-support:9.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Child support, "Changing a child support order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The Federal Child Support Guidelines set out the same circumstances for varying a child support order under the Divorce Act, and the guidelines also apply to interim orders and to orders varying a child support order. (Federal Child Support Guidelines, ss. 2 (4), 14)
```

### `guide:spousal-support:title`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Spousal support
```

### `guide:spousal-support:intro`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
This guide explains what Ontario's Family Law Act and the federal Divorce Act say about support between spouses and former spouses. It describes the law generally; it does not work out whether support is payable in any particular situation or how much.
```

### `guide:spousal-support:1:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Who is a “spouse” for support
```

### `guide:spousal-support:1.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Who is a “spouse” for support"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
In the Family Law Act, a “spouse” is either of two persons who “are married to each other”, or who “have together entered into a marriage that is voidable or void, in good faith on the part of a person relying on this clause to assert any right.” (Family Law Act, s. 1 (1))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:1.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Who is a “spouse” for support"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
For support, Part III of the Act goes further. There, “spouse” “in addition includes either of two persons who are not married to each other and have cohabited,” either “continuously for a period of not less than three years” or “in a relationship of some permanence, if they are the parents of a child as set out in section 4 of the Children’s Law Reform Act.” (Family Law Act, s. 29)
```

### `guide:spousal-support:1.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Who is a “spouse” for support"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The Act defines “cohabit” as “to live together in a conjugal relationship, whether within or outside marriage”. (Family Law Act, s. 1 (1))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:1.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Who is a “spouse” for support"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
In the Divorce Act, “spouse” “includes, in subsection 6(1) and sections 15.1 to 16.96, 21.1, 25.01 and 25.1, a former spouse”. Section 15.2 is the spousal support section. (Divorce Act, s. 2 (1))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:2:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The obligation and who can apply under the Family Law Act
```

### `guide:spousal-support:2.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "The obligation and who can apply under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The Act says: “Every spouse has an obligation to provide support for himself or herself and for the other spouse, in accordance with need, to the extent that he or she is capable of doing so.” (Family Law Act, s. 30)
```

### `guide:spousal-support:2.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "The obligation and who can apply under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
“A court may, on application, order a person to provide support for his or her dependants and determine the amount of support.” A “dependant” is “a person to whom another has an obligation to provide support under this Part”. (Family Law Act, ss. 29, 33 (1))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:2.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "The obligation and who can apply under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
An application for support of a dependant “may be made by the dependant or the dependant’s parent.” Certain government agencies may also apply for the support of a respondent’s spouse or child “if the agency is providing or has provided a benefit” of the kinds the Act lists in respect of the dependant’s support, “or if an application for such a benefit or assistance has been made to the agency by or on behalf of the dependant.” (Family Law Act, s. 33 (2), (3))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:2.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "The obligation and who can apply under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Under this Act, “court” means “the Ontario Court of Justice, the Family Court of the Superior Court of Justice or the Superior Court of Justice”. The Act also says “The Limitations Act, 2002 applies to an application made by the dependant’s parent or by an agency referred to in subsection (3) as if it were made by the dependant himself or herself.” (Family Law Act, ss. 1 (1), 33 (2.1))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:3:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
What a spousal support order should do
```

### `guide:spousal-support:3.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "What a spousal support order should do"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Under the Family Law Act, “An order for the support of a spouse should,” (a) “recognize the spouse’s contribution to the relationship and the economic consequences of the relationship for the spouse”; (b) “share the economic burden of child support equitably”; (c) “make fair provision to assist the spouse to become able to contribute to his or her own support”; and (d) “relieve financial hardship, if this has not been done by orders under Parts I (Family Property) and II (Matrimonial Home).” (Family Law Act, s. 33 (8))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:4:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
What the court considers under the Family Law Act
```

### `guide:spousal-support:4.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "What the court considers under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
“In determining the amount and duration, if any, of support for a spouse or parent in relation to need, the court shall consider all the circumstances of the parties”. The listed circumstances include each party’s “current assets and means” and those they are “likely to have in the future”, the dependant’s “capacity to contribute to his or her own support”, the respondent’s “capacity to provide support”, and their “age and physical and mental health”. (Family Law Act, s. 33 (9) (a)-(e))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:4.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "What the court considers under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The list also includes the dependant’s needs, having regard to “the accustomed standard of living while the parties resided together”; the measures available for the dependant to become self-supporting and their time and cost; other legal support obligations; “the desirability of the dependant or respondent remaining at home to care for a child”; and “a contribution by the dependant to the realization of the respondent’s career potential”. (Family Law Act, s. 33 (9) (f)-(j))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:4.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "What the court considers under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Where the dependant is a spouse, the court also considers “the length of time the dependant and respondent cohabited”, “the effect on the spouse’s earning capacity of the responsibilities assumed during cohabitation”, care or education of a child eighteen or over who cannot withdraw from the parents’ charge, “any housekeeping, child care or other domestic service performed by the spouse for the family”, and “the effect on the spouse’s earnings and career development of the responsibility of caring for a child”. (Family Law Act, s. 33 (9) (l))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:4.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "What the court considers under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
It also considers “any housekeeping, child care or other domestic service performed by the spouse for the family, as if the spouse were devoting the time spent in performing that service in remunerative employment and were contributing the earnings to the family’s support”. (Family Law Act, s. 33 (9) (l) (v))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:4.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "What the court considers under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The last listed item is “any other legal right of the dependant to support, other than out of public money.” (Family Law Act, s. 33 (9) (m))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:4.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "What the court considers under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
On conduct, the Act says “The obligation to provide support for a spouse exists without regard to the conduct of either spouse”. However, in setting the amount the court may consider “a course of conduct that is so unconscionable as to constitute an obvious and gross repudiation of the relationship.” (Family Law Act, s. 33 (10))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:5:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Kinds of support orders under the Family Law Act
```

### `guide:spousal-support:5.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Kinds of support orders under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
On a support application the court “may make an interim or final order”. Among other things, it may require “that an amount be paid periodically, whether annually or otherwise and whether for an indefinite or limited period, or until the happening of a specified event”, “that a lump sum be paid or held in trust”, or “that support be paid in respect of any period before the date of the order”. (Family Law Act, s. 34 (1) (a), (b), (f))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:5.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Kinds of support orders under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The court may also order property transferred to the dependant, require a spouse with life insurance or a pension or benefit plan to name the other spouse or a child as beneficiary, and require “the securing of payment under the order, by a charge on property or otherwise.” (Family Law Act, s. 34 (1) (c), (i), (j), (k))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:5.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Kinds of support orders under the Family Law Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The Ontario Court of Justice “shall not make an order under clause (1) (b), (c), (i), (j) or (k) except for the provision of necessities or to prevent the dependant from becoming or continuing to be a public charge, and shall not make an order under clause (d).” Clause (d) is an order respecting matrimonial home matters under clause 24 (1) (a), (b), (c), (d) or (e). (Family Law Act, s. 34 (1) (d), (2))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:6:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Spousal support under the Divorce Act
```

### `guide:spousal-support:6.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Spousal support under the Divorce Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Under the Divorce Act, a court “may, on application by either or both spouses, make an order requiring a spouse to secure or pay, or to secure and pay, such lump sum or periodic sums, or such lump sum and periodic sums, as the court thinks reasonable for the support of the other spouse.” The court may also make an interim order while the application is pending. (Divorce Act, s. 15.2 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:6.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Spousal support under the Divorce Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
An order may be “for a definite or indefinite period or until a specified event occurs”, and the court “may impose terms, conditions or restrictions in connection with the order as it thinks fit and just.” (Divorce Act, s. 15.2 (3))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:6.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Spousal support under the Divorce Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The court “shall take into consideration the condition, means, needs and other circumstances of each spouse, including” (a) “the length of time the spouses cohabited”; (b) “the functions performed by each spouse during cohabitation”; and (c) “any order, agreement or arrangement relating to support of either spouse.” (Divorce Act, s. 15.2 (4))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:6.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Spousal support under the Divorce Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
The court “shall not take into consideration any misconduct of a spouse in relation to the marriage.” (Divorce Act, s. 15.2 (5))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:6.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Spousal support under the Divorce Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
An order “should” (a) “recognize any economic advantages or disadvantages to the spouses arising from the marriage or its breakdown”; (b) “apportion between the spouses any financial consequences arising from the care of any child of the marriage”, over and above child support; (c) “relieve any economic hardship of the spouses arising from the breakdown of the marriage”; and (d) “in so far as practicable, promote the economic self-sufficiency of each spouse within a reasonable period of time.” (Divorce Act, s. 15.2 (6))
```

### `guide:spousal-support:6.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Spousal support, "Spousal support under the Divorce Act"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
Where a court has applications for both child support and spousal support, it “shall give priority to child support in determining the applications.” If that reduces or prevents spousal support, a later reduction or end of child support “constitutes a change of circumstances” for applying for spousal support or a variation. (Divorce Act, s. 15.3 (1), (3))
```

```
Marriage contracts, cohabitation agreements and separation agreements are kinds of “domestic contract”, and each may deal with “support obligations”. A domestic contract is “unenforceable unless made in writing, signed by the parties and witnessed.” (Family Law Act, ss. 51, 52 (1) (b), 53 (1) (b), 54 (b), 55 (1))
```

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Dividing property when a marriage ends
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03

```
This guide explains what Part I of Ontario's Family Law Act says about sharing the value of property when spouses separate, divorce or a spouse dies, and what the Family Law Rules require parties to disclose. It describes the law generally; it does not calculate anyone's entitlement.
```

### `guide:property-division:1:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** family / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Dividing property when a marriage ends
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90f03
