### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:intro`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
This guide explains what Ontario's Insurance Act says about accident benefits, disputes about those benefits, limits on suing for injuries from a car accident, property damage claims, uninsured vehicles, and the notice and time limits the Act sets. It covers only what the Act itself says; the regulations it refers to are not covered because the site does not yet have a source for them.
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:1:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Statutory accident benefits
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:1.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Statutory accident benefits"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Accident benefits are set out in a separate schedule. The Act says every contract evidenced by a motor vehicle liability policy “shall be deemed to provide for the statutory accident benefits set out in the Schedule and any amendments to the Schedule”. Those benefits are “subject to the terms, conditions, provisions, exclusions and limits set out in that Schedule”. (Insurance Act, s. 268 (1))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:1.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Statutory accident benefits"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
There is an exception for public transit. The Act says “no statutory accident benefits are payable in respect of an occupant of a public transit vehicle” for an incident on or after that rule came into force “if the public transit vehicle did not collide with another automobile or any other object in the incident”. (Insurance Act, s. 268 (1.1))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:1.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Statutory accident benefits"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
The Statutory Accident Benefits Schedule itself sets out what the benefits are and who qualifies. The site does not yet have a source for the Schedule, so this guide does not describe the benefits in detail. (Insurance Act, s. 268 (1))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:2:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Disputes about accident benefits go to the Licence Appeal Tribunal
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:2.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Disputes about accident benefits go to the Licence Appeal Tribunal"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Section 280 deals with disputes “in respect of an insured person's entitlement to statutory accident benefits or in respect of the amount of statutory accident benefits to which an insured person is entitled”. For those disputes, “The insured person or the insurer may apply to the Licence Appeal Tribunal to resolve a dispute described in subsection (1).” (Insurance Act, s. 280 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:2.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Disputes about accident benefits go to the Licence Appeal Tribunal"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
These disputes do not start in a court. The Act says: “No person may bring a proceeding in any court with respect to a dispute described in subsection (1), other than an appeal from a decision of the Licence Appeal Tribunal or an application for judicial review.” It also says “The dispute shall be resolved in accordance with the Statutory Accident Benefits Schedule.” (Insurance Act, s. 280 (3), (4))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:2.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Disputes about accident benefits go to the Licence Appeal Tribunal"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
After the Tribunal decides, “the insurer shall not reduce benefits to the insured person on the basis of an alleged change of circumstances, alleged new evidence or an alleged error except as provided under this section.” The insurer may reduce benefits if “the insured person agrees”, after “a successful appeal of the Licence Appeal Tribunal's decision”, or if it is “authorized to do so by the Licence Appeal Tribunal”. (Insurance Act, s. 281)
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:2.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Disputes about accident benefits go to the Licence Appeal Tribunal"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
The Act leaves the Tribunal's orders and powers to the regulations. The site does not yet have a source for the Tribunal's own rules or for any time limit to apply to it, so those are not covered here. (Insurance Act, s. 280 (5), (6))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:3:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Telling your insurer about an accident
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:3.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Telling your insurer about an accident"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
If an insured automobile is involved in an incident “that is required to be reported to the police under the Highway Traffic Act or in respect of which the insured intends to make a claim under the contract”, the insured “shall give the insurer written notice of the incident, with all available particulars.” (Insurance Act, s. 258.1 (1))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:3.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Telling your insurer about an accident"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
The notice “shall be given to the insurer within seven days of the incident.” If the insured cannot do this “because of incapacity”, the insured “shall comply as soon as possible thereafter.” (Insurance Act, s. 258.1 (2), (3))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:4:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Steps before suing for injuries
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:4.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Steps before suing for injuries"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Sections 258.3 to 258.6 apply “only in respect of a claim for loss or damage from bodily injury or death arising from the use or operation” of an automobile “in Canada, the United States of America or a jurisdiction designated in the Statutory Accident Benefits Schedule”, after section 29 of the Automobile Insurance Rate Stability Act, 1996 came into force. Under section 258.3, such an action “shall not be commenced unless” certain steps have happened. (Insurance Act, ss. 258.2, 258.3 (1))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:4.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Steps before suing for injuries"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
First, “the plaintiff has applied for statutory accident benefits”. Second, the plaintiff “served written notice of the intention to commence the action on the defendant within 120 days after the incident”, or within a longer period a court may authorize “on motion made before or after the expiry of the 120-day period”. Third, the plaintiff provided the defendant with “the information prescribed by the regulations within the time period prescribed by the regulations”. (Insurance Act, s. 258.3 (1) (a)-(c))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:4.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Steps before suing for injuries"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
If the defendant requests them “within 90 days after receiving the notice”, the plaintiff undergoes examinations, at the defendant's expense, “by one or more persons selected by the defendant who are members of Colleges as defined in the Regulated Health Professions Act, 1991”. If the defendant requests them, the plaintiff also provides “a statutory declaration describing the circumstances surrounding the incident and the nature of the claim being made” and “evidence of the plaintiff's identity”. (Insurance Act, s. 258.3 (1) (d)-(f))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:4.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Steps before suing for injuries"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
These steps have consequences but are not an absolute bar. The Act says “a person may commence an action without complying with subsection (1)”, but the court shall consider the non-compliance in awarding costs. Also, “no prejudgment interest shall be awarded under section 128 of the Courts of Justice Act for any period of time before the plaintiff served the notice under clause (1) (b).” (Insurance Act, s. 258.3 (8), (9))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:4.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Steps before suing for injuries"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
An insured who receives the notice “shall give a copy of the notice to the insurer within seven days of receiving the notice”, or, if unable “because of incapacity”, “as soon as possible thereafter.” An insurer that receives the notice “shall promptly inform the plaintiff whether there is a motor vehicle liability policy issued by the insurer to the defendant” and, if so, “the liability limits under the policy” and “whether the insurer will respond under the policy to the claim.” (Insurance Act, ss. 258.3 (2), (3), 258.4)
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:5:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Limits on suing for injuries
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:5.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Limits on suing for injuries"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Section 267.5 protects “the owner of an automobile, the occupants of an automobile and any person present at the incident” from some kinds of damages. They “are not liable in an action in Ontario” for “Damages for income loss suffered in the seven days after the incident.” (Insurance Act, s. 267.5 (1), para. 1)
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:5.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Limits on suing for injuries"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
For income loss after the first seven days and before trial, they are not liable for damages “in excess of 70 per cent of the amount of gross income that is lost during that period, as determined in accordance with the regulations.” The same 70 per cent limit applies to “loss of earning capacity” before trial. (Insurance Act, s. 267.5 (1), paras. 2, 3)
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:5.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Limits on suing for injuries"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
For health care expenses and for “non-pecuniary loss”, those persons are not liable “unless as a result of the use or operation of the automobile the injured person has died or has sustained”, (a) “permanent serious disfigurement”; or (b) “permanent serious impairment of an important physical, mental or psychological function”. (Insurance Act, s. 267.5 (3), (5))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:5.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Limits on suing for injuries"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Where damages for non-pecuniary loss can be awarded against a “protected defendant”, the court first determines the amount “without regard to this Part”, then reduces it. For damages other than under clause 61 (2) (e) of the Family Law Act, the reduction is “the greater of, A. $15,000, and B. the amount prescribed by the regulations”. For damages under that clause, it is the greater of “$7,500” and the amount prescribed by the regulations. (Insurance Act, s. 267.5 (7))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:5.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Limits on suing for injuries"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
These reductions do not apply if the damages would exceed an amount set under subsections (8.3) and (8.4), which is revised every January 1 by the published indexation percentage. They also do not apply to damages for non-pecuniary loss “awarded in respect of a person who dies as a direct or indirect result of an incident that occurs after August 31, 2010.” (Insurance Act, s. 267.5 (8), (8.1), (8.1.1), (8.3), (8.4))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:5.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Limits on suing for injuries"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
These protections have exceptions. They do not protect a person defended “by an insurer that is not licensed to undertake automobile insurance in Ontario unless the insurer has filed an undertaking under section 226.1.” For an incident on or after that rule came into force, they also do not protect “the owner or driver of a public transit vehicle if it did not collide with another automobile or any other object in the incident.” (Insurance Act, s. 267.5 (6), (6.1))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:6:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Damage to a car: direct compensation
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:6.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Damage to a car: direct compensation"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Section 263 applies when a car or its contents is damaged “arising directly or indirectly from the use or operation in Ontario of one or more other automobiles”, the damaged car is insured by an insurer licensed in Ontario (or one that has filed an undertaking), and “at least one other automobile involved in the accident” is insured the same way. (Insurance Act, s. 263 (1))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:6.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Damage to a car: direct compensation"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
When it applies, “an insured is entitled to recover for the damages to the insured's automobile and its contents and for loss of use from the insured's insurer under the coverage described in subsection 239 (1) as though the insured were a third party.” Recovery “shall be based on the degree of fault of the insurer's insured as determined under the fault determination rules.” (Insurance Act, s. 263 (2), (3))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:6.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Damage to a car: direct compensation"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
When section 263 applies, an insured cannot sue the other people involved for this damage. The Act says “an insured has no right of action against any person involved in the incident other than the insured's insurer for damages to the insured's automobile or its contents or for loss of use”. (Insurance Act, s. 263 (5) (a))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:6.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Damage to a car: direct compensation"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
An insured may sue their own insurer “if the insured is not satisfied that the degree of fault established under the fault determination rules accurately reflects the actual degree of fault or the insured is not satisfied with a proposed settlement”. Then “the matters in issue shall be determined in accordance with the ordinary rules of law.” (Insurance Act, s. 263 (4))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:6.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Damage to a car: direct compensation"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Section 263 does not apply in some situations, including “if both automobiles are owned by the same person”, to contents “being carried for reward”, and to damage to an automobile owned by the insured, or its contents, “if the damage is caused by the insured while driving another automobile.” (Insurance Act, s. 263 (7), (9), (10))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:6.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Damage to a car: direct compensation"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
An insured may elect, under the regulations, “not to recover damages from the insured's insurer under subsection (2).” If the insured makes that election, then, in addition to the restrictions in subsection (5), the insured “has no right of action under subsection (2) against the insured's insurer” for this damage or loss of use, and the insurer “shall not issue or offer collision or upset coverage” to the insured. (Insurance Act, s. 263 (2.2), (2.3))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:6.7`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Damage to a car: direct compensation"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
A proceeding against an insurer about damage to a car or its contents has its own time limit: it “shall be commenced within one year after the happening of the loss or damage.” (Insurance Act, s. 259.1)
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:7:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Uninsured and unidentified automobiles
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:7.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Uninsured and unidentified automobiles"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
Every motor vehicle liability policy “shall provide for payment of all sums that” a person insured under the contract “is legally entitled to recover from the owner or driver of an uninsured automobile or unidentified automobile as damages for bodily injuries resulting from an accident involving an automobile”, “subject to the terms, conditions, provisions, exclusions and limits as are prescribed by the regulations.” (Insurance Act, s. 265 (1) (a))
```

### `guide:car-accidents-and-insurance:7.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Car accidents and insurance, "Uninsured and unidentified automobiles"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90i08

```
It also covers sums a person insured under the contract can recover “from the identified owner or driver of an uninsured automobile as damages for accidental damage to the insured automobile or its contents”. All of this is “subject to the terms, conditions, provisions, exclusions and limits as are prescribed by the regulations.” The site does not yet have a source for those regulations. (Insurance Act, s. 265 (1) (c))
```

```
Condominium disputes
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:intro`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
This guide explains what Ontario's Condominium Act, 1998 and the Condominium Authority of Ontario say about condo disputes: the Condominium Authority Tribunal, the duty to follow the Act and the condo's documents, compliance orders in the Superior Court of Justice, and common expenses and liens. The regulation that lists which disputes the Tribunal hears is not covered, because the site does not yet have a source for it.
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:1:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
What the Condominium Authority Tribunal is
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:1.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "What the Condominium Authority Tribunal is"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
In this part of the Act, “Tribunal” means “the Condominium Authority Tribunal established under subsection 1.32 (1).” The Condominium Authority of Ontario describes it as “Canada’s first fully online tribunal”. (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 1.31; condoauthorityontario.ca, Condominium Authority Tribunal — Dispute Resolution)
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:1.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "What the Condominium Authority Tribunal is"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
The Authority says: “Regulation 179/17 defines the scope of disputes that can be resolved by the Tribunal.” The site does not yet have a copy of that regulation, so this guide does not list the types of disputes it covers. (condoauthorityontario.ca, Condominium Authority Tribunal — Dispute Resolution)
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:1.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "What the Condominium Authority Tribunal is"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
Subject to one exception, “the Tribunal has exclusive jurisdiction to exercise the powers conferred on it under this Act and to determine all questions of fact or law that arise in any proceeding before it.” The exception: it “shall not inquire into or make a decision concerning the constitutional validity of a provision of an Act or a regulation.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 1.42)
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:2:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
Who can apply to the Tribunal, and about what
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:2.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Who can apply to the Tribunal, and about what"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
A condo corporation “may apply to the Tribunal for the resolution of a prescribed dispute with one or more of its owners or one or more occupiers or mortgagees of a unit.” An owner or a mortgagee of a unit “may apply to the Tribunal for the resolution of a prescribed dispute with the corporation, another owner or an occupier or a mortgagee of a unit.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 1.36 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:2.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Who can apply to the Tribunal, and about what"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
If the regulations so provide, a purchaser may apply about a dispute with the corporation regarding compliance with subsection 55 (3), “but not any other dispute.” An application “shall be in the form approved by the Tribunal.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 1.36 (3), (5))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:2.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Who can apply to the Tribunal, and about what"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
Some disputes cannot go to the Tribunal. These include a dispute about “Part III, section 20, 26, 82.1, 82.2, 85 or 86, subsection 117 (1) or Part VII or VIII”, and “a dispute involving the determination of title to any real property.” Sections 85 and 86 deal with the condo lien described below. (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 1.36 (4))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:3:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
Time limits for Tribunal applications
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:3.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Time limits for Tribunal applications"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
“Subject to any other provision of this Act, an application must be made within two years after the dispute to which the application relates arose.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 1.36 (6))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:3.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Time limits for Tribunal applications"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
If that deadline is missed, “the Tribunal may extend the deadline for a time of no more than one additional year if the Tribunal is satisfied that the delay in not applying was incurred in good faith and no substantial prejudice will result to any person affected by the delay.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 1.36 (7))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:3.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Time limits for Tribunal applications"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
Parties can settle. A signed written settlement “is binding on the parties.” A party who believes another party has broken the settlement may apply to the Tribunal “within six months after the contravention to which the application relates”, or later if the Tribunal is satisfied the delay “was incurred in good faith and no substantial prejudice will result to any person affected by the delay.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 1.47 (1), (3))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:4:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
How a Tribunal case runs, and what it can order
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:4.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "How a Tribunal case runs, and what it can order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
A Tribunal proceeding “may be held orally or in writing, in person, by telephone, video conference or electronic mail, or through use of other electronic means in accordance with the rules of the Tribunal.” The Tribunal may direct the parties to take part in an “alternative dispute resolution mechanism”, which “includes mediation, conciliation, negotiation or any other means of facilitating the resolution of issues in dispute.” (Condominium Act, 1998, ss. 1.39 (2), 1.40)
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:4.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "How a Tribunal case runs, and what it can order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
The Tribunal may refuse to allow a person to make an application, or may dismiss an application without holding a hearing, if it “is of the opinion that the subject matter of the application is frivolous or vexatious or that the application has not been initiated in good faith or discloses no reasonable cause of action.” It may also dismiss without a hearing if the applicant filed documents “that the applicant knew or ought to have known to have contained false or misleading information.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 1.41)
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:4.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "How a Tribunal case runs, and what it can order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
Orders the Tribunal may make include an order “prohibiting a party to the proceeding from taking a particular action or requiring a party to the proceeding to take a particular action”, and an order to pay “compensation for damages incurred by another party to the proceeding as a result of an act of non-compliance up to the greater of $25,000 or the amount, if any, that is prescribed.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 1.44 (1))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:4.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "How a Tribunal case runs, and what it can order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
The Tribunal may also order a party to pay the costs of another party or the costs of the Tribunal. Those costs are determined “in accordance with the rules of the Tribunal.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 1.44 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:4.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "How a Tribunal case runs, and what it can order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
The Tribunal “shall not make an order requiring a person to vacate a property permanently.” The party against whom an order for compensation, costs or a penalty is made pays the amount “within 30 days, unless the order specifies another time limit.” (Condominium Act, 1998, ss. 1.44 (4), 1.45 (1))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:4.6`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "How a Tribunal case runs, and what it can order"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
A Tribunal order “is final and binding”, except that a party “may appeal the order to the Divisional Court on a question of law in accordance with the rules of court.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 1.46 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:5:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
The duty to follow the Act, declaration, by-laws and rules
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:5.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "The duty to follow the Act, declaration, by-laws and rules"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
A condo corporation's objects “are to manage the property and the assets, if any, of the corporation on behalf of the owners.” It “has a duty to take all reasonable steps to ensure that the owners, the occupiers of units, the lessees of the common elements and the agents and employees of the corporation comply with this Act, the declaration, the by-laws and the rules.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 17 (1), (3))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:5.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "The duty to follow the Act, declaration, by-laws and rules"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
The corporation, its directors, officers and employees, the declarant, an owner, an occupier of a unit and others listed “shall comply with this Act, the declaration, the by-laws and the rules.” An owner “shall take all reasonable steps to ensure that an occupier of the owner's unit and all invitees, agents and employees of the owner or occupier comply”. (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 119 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:5.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "The duty to follow the Act, declaration, by-laws and rules"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
A corporation, an owner and every person with a registered mortgage against a unit “have the right to require that a person who is required to comply with this Act, the declaration, the by-laws and the rules shall do so.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 119 (3))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:6:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
Compliance orders in the Superior Court of Justice
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:6.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Compliance orders in the Superior Court of Justice"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
An owner, a corporation, a mortgagee of a unit and others listed “may make an application to the Superior Court of Justice for an order enforcing compliance with any provision of this Act, the declaration, the by-laws, the rules” or certain agreements between corporations. (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 134 (1))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:6.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Compliance orders in the Superior Court of Justice"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
This court route does not apply “to any matter in dispute for which a person may apply for resolution under section 1.36 to the Condominium Authority Tribunal established under Part I.2, if the Tribunal has been established under that Part.” Also, if the mediation and arbitration processes in section 132 are required, a person may not apply “until the person has failed to obtain compliance through using those processes.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 134 (2), (2.4))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:6.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Compliance orders in the Superior Court of Justice"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
On an application, the court may “grant the order applied for”, require payment of “the damages incurred by the applicant as a result of the acts of non-compliance” and “the costs incurred by the applicant in obtaining the order”, or “grant such other relief as is fair and equitable in the circumstances.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 134 (3))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:6.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Compliance orders in the Superior Court of Justice"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
One limit on those orders: the court may not grant an order terminating a lease of a unit for residential purposes unless it is satisfied that “the lessee is in contravention of an order that has been made under subsection (3)”, or that the lessee has received a notice described in subsection 87 (1) and “has not paid the amount required by that subsection.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 134 (4))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:6.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** civil / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Compliance orders in the Superior Court of Justice"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
If a corporation obtains an award of damages or costs against an owner or occupier of a unit, those amounts, “together with any additional actual costs to the corporation in obtaining the order, shall be added to the common expenses for the unit”, and the corporation may specify a time for payment by the owner. (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 134 (5))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:7:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
Common expenses and condo liens
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:7.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Common expenses and condo liens"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
“Subject to the other provisions of this Act, the owners shall contribute to the common expenses in the proportions specified in the declaration.” An owner is not exempt even if the owner “has waived or abandoned the right to use the common elements or part of them”, “the owner is making a claim against the corporation”, or the declaration, by-laws or rules restrict the owner's use. (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 84 (1), (3))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:7.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Common expenses and condo liens"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
If an owner defaults, “the corporation has a lien against the owner's unit and its appurtenant common interest for the unpaid amount together with all interest owing and all reasonable legal costs and reasonable expenses incurred by the corporation in connection with the collection or attempted collection of the unpaid amount.” (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 85 (1))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:7.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Common expenses and condo liens"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
“The lien expires three months after the default that gave rise to the lien occurred unless the corporation within that time registers a certificate of lien in a form prescribed by the Minister.” “At least 10 days before the day a certificate of lien is registered, the corporation shall give written notice of the lien to the owner”. (Condominium Act, 1998, s. 85 (2), (4))
```

### `guide:condo-disputes:7.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Condominium disputes, "Common expenses and condo liens"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/98c19

```
“The lien may be enforced in the same manner as a mortgage.” Upon payment of the amounts the certificate covers, the corporation “shall prepare and register a discharge of the certificate of lien” and advise the owner in writing of the particulars of the registration. A dispute about section 85 or 86 cannot be brought to the Tribunal. (Condominium Act, 1998, ss. 85 (6), (7), 1.36 (4))
```

```
Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment
```

### `guide:construction-liens:intro`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
This guide explains what Ontario's Construction Act says about who can claim a construction lien, holdbacks, the time limits for preserving and perfecting a lien, where lien actions are heard, prompt payment and adjudication. Numbers are given exactly as the Act states them.
```

### `guide:construction-liens:1:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
Who can claim a lien
```

### `guide:construction-liens:1.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment, "Who can claim a lien"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
“A person who supplies services or materials to an improvement for an owner, contractor or subcontractor, has a lien upon the interest of the owner in the premises improved for the price of those services or materials.” (Construction Act, s. 14 (1))
```

### `guide:construction-liens:1.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment, "Who can claim a lien"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
An “improvement” means, in respect of any land, “any alteration, addition or capital repair to the land”, “any construction, erection or installation on the land” (including some equipment the Act describes), or “the complete or partial demolition or removal of any building, structure or works on the land”. (Construction Act, s. 1 (1), “improvement”)
```

### `guide:construction-liens:1.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment, "Who can claim a lien"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
“A person's lien arises and takes effect when the person first supplies services or materials to the improvement.” No person is entitled to a lien “for any interest on the amount owed to the person”, but this does not affect any right the person may otherwise have to recover that interest. (Construction Act, ss. 15, 14 (2))
```

### `guide:construction-liens:1.4`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment, "Who can claim a lien"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
A lien “does not attach to the interest in a premises of”, “the Crown” or “a municipality”. Where either has an interest in a premises but is not an owner, “the lien may attach to the interest of any other person in the premises.” Where the owner is the Crown or a municipality, or the premises is a railway right-of-way, the lien does not attach to the premises but “constitutes a charge under section 21”. (Construction Act, s. 16)
```

### `guide:construction-liens:1.5`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment, "Who can claim a lien"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
These rules do not apply to every project. The Act and regulations “as they read on June 29, 2018, continue to apply” to an improvement if, for example, “a contract for the improvement was entered into before July 1, 2018” or the owner commenced a procurement process for it before that date. The prompt payment and adjudication Parts (I.1 and II.1) also do not apply to certain older contracts and their subcontracts, as the Act lists. (Construction Act, s. 87.3 (1), (4))
```

### `guide:construction-liens:2:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
Holdbacks
```

### `guide:construction-liens:2.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment, "Holdbacks"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
“Each payer upon a contract or subcontract under which a lien may arise shall retain a holdback equal to 10 per cent of the price of the services or materials as they are actually supplied under the contract or subcontract until all liens that may be claimed against the holdback in respect of the supplied services or materials have expired or been satisfied, discharged or otherwise provided for under this Act.” (Construction Act, s. 22 (1))
```

### `guide:construction-liens:2.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment, "Holdbacks"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
Where a contract has been certified or declared substantially performed but work remains, the payer keeps “a separate holdback equal to 10 per cent of the price of the remaining services or materials”. The duty to keep holdbacks applies “irrespective of whether the contract or subcontract provides for partial payments or payment on completion.” (Construction Act, s. 22 (2), (3))
```

### `guide:construction-liens:2.3`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment, "Holdbacks"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
Subject to limits, an owner “is personally liable for holdbacks that the owner is required to retain under this Part to those lien claimants who have valid liens against the owner's interest in the premises.” Where the defaulting payer is the contractor, that liability “does not exceed the holdbacks the owner is required to retain”. Where it is a subcontractor, a lower cap can apply. This liability “may only be determined by an action under this Act.” (Construction Act, s. 23)
```

### `guide:construction-liens:3:heading`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
Preserving a lien and the time limits
```

### `guide:construction-liens:3.1`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment, "Preserving a lien and the time limits"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
“Unless preserved under section 34, the liens arising from the supply of services or materials to an improvement expire as provided in this section.” (Construction Act, s. 31 (1))
```

### `guide:construction-liens:3.2`

- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment, "Preserving a lien and the time limits"
- **Source:** https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/90c30

```
A contractor's lien for work up to substantial performance “expires at the conclusion of the 60-day period next following the occurrence of the earlier of” the date a copy of the certificate or declaration of substantial performance “is published as provided in section 32”, and “the date the contract is completed, abandoned or terminated”. (Construction Act, s. 31 (2) (a))
```

### `guide:construction-liens:3.3`

Where it does not attach, it is perfected when the claimant “commences an action to enforce the lien.” A preserved lien can also be perfected by “sheltering” under another claimant's perfected lien, under the rules in the Act.
```
A “proper invoice” is “a written bill or other request for payment for services or materials in respect of an improvement under a contract” that contains information the Act lists, such as the contractor's name and address, the invoice date and a description of what was supplied, and, “subject to subsection 6.3 (2)”, meets any other requirements the contract specifies. (Construction Act, s. 6.1 (1))
```

- **Status:** draft

```
“Proper invoices shall be given to an owner on a monthly basis, unless the contract provides otherwise.” A contract term that makes giving a proper invoice “conditional on the prior certification of a payment certifier or on the owner's prior approval is of no force or effect.” (Construction Act, s. 6.3 (1), (2))
```

### `guide:construction-liens:6.3`

- **Status:** draft


### `guide:construction-liens:6.4`

- **Status:** draft

- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment, "Prompt payment"

```
Subject to a notice of non-payment, an owner “shall pay the amount payable under a proper invoice no later than 28 days after receiving the proper invoice from the contractor.” An owner who disputes an invoice may refuse to pay if, “no later than 14 days after receiving the proper invoice”, it gives a notice of non-payment, in the prescribed form and manner, “specifying the amount of the proper invoice that is not being paid and detailing all of the reasons for non-payment.” (Construction Act, s. 6.4 (1), (2))
```

- **Status:** draft


- **Status:** draft
- **Pathway / stage:** all / guide
- **Appears in:** Guides, Construction liens, holdbacks and prompt payment, "Prompt payment"

```
A contractor who receives full payment of a proper invoice within those 28 days pays each subcontractor whose services or materials were in the invoice “no later than seven days after receiving payment”. If the owner pays only part, the contractor pays those subcontractors from the amount paid, within the same seven days. Both are subject to a notice of non-payment and, like every payment under this Part, “subject to any requirement to retain a holdback”. (Construction Act, ss. 6.2, 6.5 (1), (2))
```

```
If the owner does not pay some or all of a proper invoice on time, the contractor pays those subcontractors “no later than 35 days after giving the proper invoice to the owner”, unless it gives a notice of non-payment. A notice given because the owner has not paid must include “an undertaking to refer the matter to adjudication under Part II.1 no later than 21 days after giving the notice to the subcontractor”. (Construction Act, s. 6.5 (4), (5))
```

Similar rules apply between subcontractors. (Construction Act, ss. 6.5 (6), (7), 6.6)
```

“Adjudication” means “construction dispute interim adjudication under this Part”. A party to a contract “may refer a dispute with the other party to the contract respecting any prescribed matter or any matter agreed to by the parties to adjudication.” The same applies to a subcontract. ```
```
```
For a contract, adjudication “may not be commenced if the notice of adjudication is given more than 90 days after the date on which the contract is completed, abandoned or terminated, unless the parties to the adjudication agree otherwise.” For a subcontract, the 90 days run from the earliest of that date, “the date on which the subcontract is certified to be completed under section 33”, and “the date on which the subcontractor last supplies services or materials to the improvement.” (Construction Act, s. 13.5 (3), (3.1))
```

```
A dispute may be referred to adjudication “even if the dispute is the subject of a court action or of an arbitration under the Arbitration Act, 1991, unless the action or arbitration has been finally determined.” An adjudication may only address a single dispute, unless the parties and the adjudicator agree otherwise. (Construction Act, s. 13.5 (4), (5))
```

```
Except as provided by the regulations, a written notice of adjudication includes the parties' names and addresses, “the nature and a brief description of the dispute, including details respecting how and when it arose”, “the nature of the redress sought”, “the name of a proposed adjudicator to conduct the adjudication”, and “the date, nature and substance of any previous adjudication in which the party was involved in respect of the contract or subcontract, including a copy of any determination made by the adjudicator.” (Construction Act, s. 13.7 (1))
```

```
The adjudicator decides “no later than 30 days after receiving the documents required by section 13.11”. Before it expires, and after those documents are provided, that deadline may be extended on the adjudicator's request, with the parties' written consent, for “no more than 14 days”, or by the parties' written agreement, with the adjudicator's consent, “for the period specified in the agreement.” A determination made after the deadline “is of no force or effect.” (Construction Act, s. 13.13 (1), (2), (5))
```

```
The determination “is binding on the parties to the adjudication until a determination of the matter by a court”, an arbitration under the Arbitration Act, 1991, or a written agreement between the parties. A party required to pay “shall pay the amount no later than 15 days after the determination has been communicated to the parties to the adjudication”, subject to any requirement to retain a holdback. (Construction Act, ss. 13.15 (1), 13.19 (1), (2))
```

```
Judicial review of a determination “may only be made with leave of the Divisional Court”, and the motion for leave is filed, with proof of service, “no later than 35 days after the determination is communicated to the parties.” The determination may only be set aside on the grounds the Act lists. An application for judicial review “does not operate as a stay of the operation of the determination unless the Divisional Court orders otherwise.” (Construction Act, s. 13.18 (1), (2), (5), (7))
```

```
Subject to section 13.17, the parties “shall bear their own costs of the adjudication.” Under section 13.17, if the adjudicator determines a party acted in a manner that is “frivolous, vexatious, an abuse of process or other than in good faith”, the adjudicator may require that party to pay some or all of the other party's costs, part of the adjudicator's fee the other party would otherwise pay, or both. (Construction Act, ss. 13.16, 13.17)
```
